- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## DEVONthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

## omnifocus
OmniFocus is a GTD task manager. Hierarchy: Folders > Projects > Tasks > Subtasks.

TASK STATES: Available, Blocked, Deferred (future defer date), Flagged, Overdue, Completed, Dropped. Planned Date is a scheduling signal only — no availability/overdue constraints.

PROJECT TYPES: "sequential" (tasks in order; first incomplete = available, rest blocked; position = dependencies), "parallel" (all available), "single_actions" (no completion goal, cannot auto-complete). The `next` field is true for the first available action in a sequential project/action group; in parallel projects, all incomplete tasks have `next: true`.

ACTION GROUPS: Task with subtasks. Parent shows `blocked: true` while subtasks are active — this is normal, not an error. Do not try to unblock it.

INHERITED STATUS: `completed`/`dropped` reflect the task's own state, not its container's. `effectivelyCompleted`/`effectivelyDropped` reflect the container's state — if true, the task's parent project or action group was completed/dropped. Task in completed project: `completed: false`, `effectivelyCompleted: true`, `available: false`. Use `available_only=True` for actionable tasks.

EFFECTIVE DATES: Dates returned by get_tasks are always effective (inherited). A task with no direct due date WILL show its project's due date in the dueDate field — this is correct behavior, not a bug. You cannot clear an inherited date at the task level. Write operations set the task's own date.

RECURRING TASKS: `completed=True` uses `mark complete`, which creates the next occurrence. This is guaranteed. WARNING: Dropping a recurring task (status='dropped') without clearing recurrence first (recurrence='') spawns the next occurrence. To stop a series: update_tasks([{"id": "...", "recurrence": "", "status": "dropped"}]).

TAGS: Represent work contexts. Tag statuses: Active (normal), On Hold (tasks excluded from Available perspective), Dropped (tag hidden from picker; does NOT affect task availability).

DEFER vs DUE: Defer = hidden until that date. Due = deadline.

- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- grilling: Grill the user relentlessly about a plan or design. Use when the user wants to stress-test a plan before building, or uses any 'grill' trigger phrases.
- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
- seo-optimizer: Optimize content for search engines with keyword analysis, readability scoring, meta descriptions, and competitor comparison. Use this when users want to improve SEO, optimize blog posts, or analyze content for search performance.
- systems-thinking: Analyze problems using a Systems Thinking approach. Use when users mention "systems thinking," "systemic," "feedback loops," "unintended consequences," "root cause," "interconnected," or request analysis of complex, multi-factor problems. Guides conversation through questions and observations rather than prescriptive solutions.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.
- copilot-fetch-x: Fetch the content of an X (Twitter) post using Copilot Plus. Use when the user shares an x.com or twitter.com URL and wants its text or context. Requires an active Copilot Plus license.
- copilot-read-pdf: Extract the full text of a PDF as Markdown using Copilot Plus. Use when the user wants to read, summarize, or quote a PDF file (in the vault or an absolute path). Requires an active Copilot Plus license.
- copilot-web-fetch: Fetch and read the full contents of a specific web page (URL) as clean Markdown using Copilot Plus. Use when the user shares a link or asks you to open, read, or summarize a particular page — not for an open-ended web search. Requires an active Copilot Plus license; without it, use your own fetch tool instead.
- copilot-web-search: Search the web for current information using Copilot Plus. Use when the user asks to search online, look something up on the internet, or needs up-to-date facts beyond the vault. Prefer reading the vault for anything about the user's own notes. Requires an active Copilot Plus license.
- copilot-youtube-transcript: Fetch the transcript of a YouTube video using Copilot Plus. Use when the user shares a YouTube URL and wants its contents, a summary, or quotes. Requires an active Copilot Plus license.
- miyo-search: Semantic (meaning-based) search over the user's Obsidian vault via the local Miyo app. For any vault-search intent, use it when builtin grep search is too slow or doesn't surface enough relevant notes, or when the user explicitly asks for Miyo search. Needs the Miyo desktop app installed and running.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- claude-md-management:revise-claude-md: Update CLAUDE.md with learnings from this session
- claude-md-management:claude-md-improver: Audit and improve CLAUDE.md files in repositories. Use when user asks to check, audit, update, improve, or fix CLAUDE.md files. Scans for all CLAUDE.md files, evaluates quality against templates, outputs quality report, then makes targeted updates. Also use when the user mentions "CLAUDE.md maintenance" or "project memory optimization".
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## Skills

### Drafts Inbox
**Purpose:** Triages everything in the Drafts inbox (no longer keyed to a "cowork" tag), classifies each item, takes action, and archives when done so the inbox stays the unprocessed queue. For a large backlog, asks how far back to go and filters by `modificationDate`. Tasks route to `omnifocus-capture`.
**Triggers:** "check my Drafts inbox," "process my inbox," "what's in Drafts," "triage my Drafts inbox," "drafts inbox triage"
**File:** `Skills/drafts-inbox.md`
**Dependencies:** Drafts MCP connector; `Skills/omnifocus-capture.md` (for task capture)

### Daily Briefing
**Purpose:** Produces a morning overview of your day - calendar, unread priority/people email, tasks, deadlines.
**Triggers:** "run my briefing," "morning briefing," "what's my day look like"
**File:** `Skills/daily-briefing.md`
**Dependencies:** Calendar MCP connector (when set up), Gmail MCP connector (email step; uses `Skills/gmail-triage.md` conventions)

### Shutdown Routine
**Purpose:** Reviews the day, checks email loose ends, scans the APR + expense-tracker git repos for open loops (uncommitted/unpushed/stashed work), scans today's Claude conversations across all projects for unresolved threads, surfaces what's outstanding, previews tomorrow.
**Triggers:** "run my shutdown," "end of day," "close out the day"
**File:** `Skills/shutdown-routine.md`
**Dependencies:** Gmail MCP connector (email loose-ends step; uses `Skills/gmail-triage.md` conventions), Calendar MCP connector (tomorrow preview)

### Weekly Review
**Purpose:** A weekly check-in workflow that reviews the past week (calendar, email digest), sweeps the OmniFocus inbox (via `omnifocus-inbox-triage`) and the Drafts inbox (via `drafts-inbox`), surfaces a few Content Ideas, scans what's ahead, and produces a summary with priorities. Includes a read-only git work-recap across the APR repos (agile-pain-relief-astro, social-media-posting) summarizing what shipped, grouped by theme. In-chat only -- never saved to a file; no reflective questions. LifeHQ-Mark is excluded by a global deny rule.
**Triggers:** "weekly review," "how'd my week go," "plan my week," "Sunday review," "what did I ship this week," "weekly work summary," "recap the repos"
**File:** `Skills/weekly-review.md`
**Dependencies:** Calendar MCP connector (when set up), Gmail MCP connector (email digest), Bash git access to the APR repos (read-only) for the work-recap, `Skills/omnifocus-inbox-triage.md` (OmniFocus inbox sweep), `Skills/drafts-inbox.md` (Drafts review)

### Quarterly Review
**Purpose:** A quarterly check-in workflow that reviews the calendar quarter Mark is closing out (calendar, email volume, completed work), rolls up quarter-level analytics and marketing experiments, surfaces a few Content Ideas, scans what's ahead, and produces a summary with priorities. Includes a read-only git work-recap across the APR repos (agile-pain-relief-astro, social-media-posting) summarizing what shipped, grouped by theme. The weekly review scaled to a quarter, but **read-only** - it deliberately omits the OmniFocus inbox sweep and the Drafts cleanup. In-chat only; never saved to a file; no reflective questions. LifeHQ-Mark is excluded by a global deny rule. Window defaults to the quarter being closed out (mid-quarter → quarter start through today; early in a new quarter → the full just-ended quarter).
**Triggers:** "quarterly review," "how'd my quarter go," "plan my quarter," "quarterly work summary," "what did I ship this quarter," "recap the quarter"
**File:** `Skills/quarterly-review.md`
**Dependencies:** Calendar MCP connector (when set up), Gmail MCP connector (email digest), Bash git access to the APR repos (read-only) for the work-recap, `Skills/omnifocus-query.md` (read-only completed-work review), `Skills/apr-weekly-analytics.md` (optional fresh pull). Does **not** depend on the inbox-triage skills (cleanup steps removed).

### File Organizer
**Purpose:** Scans a folder for files that don't match your naming conventions, proposes renames and folder placement, and executes on approval.
**Triggers:** "organize these files," "sort this folder," "clean up my files," "rename these"
**File:** `Skills/file-organizer.md`
**Dependencies:** Naming conventions documented in CLAUDE.md

### Robot Assistant Assembler
**Purpose:** Personalizes the Starter Kit as you work through the video series. Each module asks questions about your work and customizes the corresponding template.
**Triggers:** "run the assembler for video [N]," "assembler for video [N]," "build video [N]"
**File:** `Skills/robot-assistant-assembler.md`
**Dependencies:** Starter Kit template files

### APR Newsletter Reviewer
**Purpose:** Reviews and critiques draft newsletters against Mark's authentic voice, tone, and style guidelines. Produces a structured critique with anti-pattern detections, terminology checks, a provisional subject-line check (filename-derived line plus any `// Subject A:` / `// Subject B:` A/B variants), and priority fixes. When the draft is a Markdown file, delivers the critique as inline CriticMarkup (see criticmarkup-editing); chat critique is the fallback for pasted text.
**Triggers:** "review my newsletter," "critique this draft," "does this sound like me," "voice check," "newsletter rubric," "style check," "review my subject line," "subject line check"
**File:** `Skills/apr-newsletter-reviewer.md`
**Dependencies:** `Skills/criticmarkup-editing.md` (delivery format)

### APR Newsletter Reading Recap
**Purpose:** Builds the "Mark's Reading Rabbit Hole" section for the newsletter — a paste-ready Markdown list of what Mark read since the last issue, linked to originals, with neutral one-line descriptions. Papers and PDFs lead; archived-without-highlights items are demoted to a short trailing list. Window defaults to "since the last newsletter" (auto-detected from the Newsletter folder). Skips any article already featured in the reading section of the last 15 issues (exclusion set derived from the newsletter files themselves, reading-section links only, URL-normalized); the window can widen further back since repeats are filtered. Read-only and print-to-chat only; never edits the newsletter file.
**Triggers:** "reading recap for the newsletter," "reading rabbit hole," "what should go in the newsletter reading list," "newsletter reading section"
**File:** `Skills/apr-newsletter-reading-recap.md`
**Dependencies:** Readwise CLI (preferred) or Readwise MCP; reads `Skills/Readwise/readwise-cli/SKILL.md` for command reference

### Log Triage
**Purpose:** Analyzes bullet points in Log.md and suggests the top 3-4 vault files where each one belongs, with confidence scores. Offers to move items on approval.
**Triggers:** "process my log," "triage my log," "sort my log entries," "where do my log notes go"
**File:** `Skills/log-triage.md`
**Dependencies:** Agents.md (vault ontology)

### OmniFocus Query
**Purpose:** Read-only queries against OmniFocus via the omnifocus MCP. Flagged, overdue, due today, stalled, inbox, search, by project or folder or tag. Also handles the "what's on my plate today" daily-plan flow.
**Triggers:** "what's in OmniFocus," "show me my flagged tasks," "what's overdue," "OmniFocus stats," "check OmniFocus," "list OmniFocus tasks," "OmniFocus inbox," "what's stalled," "what's on my plate today," "daily plan"
**File:** `Skills/omnifocus-query.md`
**Dependencies:** `omnifocus` MCP, `Skills/omnifocus-workflow.md`

### OmniFocus Capture
**Purpose:** Adds one or more tasks to OmniFocus via the omnifocus MCP. Defaults to inbox; only targets a project when Mark names one. Single writes proceed immediately, batches confirm.
**Triggers:** "capture to OmniFocus," "add to inbox," "add to OmniFocus," "capture task," "new OmniFocus task," "drop this in OmniFocus"
**File:** `Skills/omnifocus-capture.md`
**Dependencies:** `omnifocus` MCP, `Skills/omnifocus-workflow.md`

### OmniFocus Inbox Triage
**Purpose:** Walks every item in the OmniFocus inbox, proposes a project (plus optional tags, due, flag, rename) per item, and applies approved edits as a single batch update.
**Triggers:** "process my OmniFocus inbox," "triage OmniFocus," "sort my OmniFocus inbox," "clear my OmniFocus inbox," "OmniFocus inbox zero"
**File:** `Skills/omnifocus-inbox-triage.md`
**Dependencies:** `omnifocus` MCP, `Skills/omnifocus-workflow.md`

### OmniFocus Focus
**Purpose:** Narrows OmniFocus to a bucket (Personal/Family, APR, YFL) via `set_focus`, shows current focus, or clears focus. Minimal scope; perspective switching not wired in.
**Triggers:** "focus on APR," "focus on YFL," "focus on Personal," "focus on Family," "clear OmniFocus focus," "what's OmniFocus focused on"
**File:** `Skills/omnifocus-focus.md`
**Dependencies:** `omnifocus` MCP, `Skills/omnifocus-workflow.md`

### OmniFocus Workflow (shared context, not a triggered skill)
**Purpose:** Shared conventions for the four OmniFocus skills: bucket mapping, the roles-pull status-tag system (Shelf / Next Week / Weekly Plan lanes, WIP limit, Sunday pull), capture defaults, review cadence, focus design, and safety rails. Roles map to folders; Arete statements live in `Self/Roles.md`.
**File:** `Skills/omnifocus-workflow.md`
**Dependencies:** None (read by the four OmniFocus skills at runtime)

### Roles / Arete Prompts (reference, not a triggered skill)
**Purpose:** Question banks for drafting and revising Mark's roles and Arete statements in `Self/Roles.md`. Used when adding a role or reworking an Arete.
**Files:** `Skills/Roles/role-brainstorming-prompts.md`, `Skills/Roles/arete-interview-questions.md`
**Dependencies:** `Self/Roles.md` (where drafts land)

### APR Content Performance
**Purpose:** Analyze APR content performance across social media, email newsletters, and website traffic. Reads raw data from the Astro repo (`agile-pain-relief-astro/analytics/`), writes a single live snapshot to `APR/Analytics/content-performance-snapshot.md` (overwrite, not dated).
**Triggers:** "content performance," "analyze my content," "how are my posts doing," "newsletter engagement," "which topics perform best," "social to website traffic"
**File:** `Skills/apr-content-performance.md`
**Dependencies:** Bash access to Astro repo analytics folder, `APR/Efforts/Newsletter/` for matching newsletter content

### APR Competitive Landscape
**Purpose:** Competitive analysis frameworks (Porter's Five Forces, Blue Ocean, positioning maps) tailored for APR's Scrum/Agile training and GenAI-for-business-agility market. Writes new analyses to `APR/Analytics/`.
**Triggers:** "analyze competitors," "competitive landscape," "identify differentiation," "market positioning," "Porter's Five Forces"
**File:** `Skills/apr-competitive-landscape.md`
**Dependencies:** Existing APR competitive docs in `APR/Analytics/` (e.g. `genai-course-competitive-analysis.md`)

### APR Weekly Analytics
**Purpose:** Orchestrate the weekly analytics loop — run `npm run scrape` and `npm run posthog-export` in the Astro repo, invoke `apr-content-performance` to regenerate the live report, flag experiment follow-ups, capture tasks to OmniFocus.
**Triggers:** "run weekly analytics," "refresh analytics," "pull analytics," "weekly data pull"
**File:** `Skills/apr-weekly-analytics.md`
**Dependencies:** `apr-content-performance`, `omnifocus-capture`, `omnifocus-workflow`, Bash access to Astro repo

### Calendar Access
**Purpose:** Read, create, update, and delete Google Calendar events via the Google Calendar MCP. Defaults to Personal + APR Business + TripIt, adds Time Blocking for planning queries. Writes always confirm before executing.
**Triggers:** "what's on my calendar," "what's my week," "check my calendar," "add to my calendar," "reschedule," "cancel my appointment," "create an event"
**File:** `Skills/calendar-access.md`
**Dependencies:** Google Calendar MCP connector

### Calendar Audit
**Purpose:** Read-only meeting-load analysis layered on `calendar-access` — total meetings, hours, busiest/lightest days, back-to-back chains, free blocks over a week or custom range. Re-pointed from the retired Spark suite to the Google Calendar MCP.
**Triggers:** "calendar audit," "analyze my meeting load," "back-to-back check," "how busy is my week"
**File:** `Skills/calendar-audit.md`
**Dependencies:** Google Calendar MCP connector; `Skills/calendar-access.md` (default calendar set + tool list)

### Topic Timeline
**Purpose:** Builds a chronological narrative for a project/topic from email threads, optionally anchored by calendar events. Re-pointed from the retired Spark suite to the Gmail MCP; email-first now (the old Spark meeting-transcript half has no replacement, so calendar events stand in as date anchors).
**Triggers:** "topic timeline," "narrative of this project," "what happened on this topic," "catch me up on this topic"
**File:** `Skills/topic-timeline.md`
**Dependencies:** Gmail MCP connector (thread search/read); Google Calendar MCP connector (optional date anchors)

### APR LinkedIn Style
**Purpose:** Reviews and critiques draft LinkedIn posts against Mark's voice and LinkedIn-specific conventions (length, hooks, emoji, hashtags, external links). Covers Scrum/Agile posts, GenAI/LLM posts (skeptical-pragmatist lean), personal posts, and business announcements. Produces a structured critique with anti-pattern detections and prioritised improvement suggestions. Does not rewrite drafts wholesale. When the draft is a Markdown file, delivers the critique as inline CriticMarkup (see criticmarkup-editing); chat critique is the fallback for pasted text.
**Triggers:** "review this LinkedIn post," "critique my post," "LinkedIn style," "LinkedIn rubric," "post review," "does this post sound like me," "voice check on this post"
**File:** `Skills/apr-linkedin-style.md`
**Dependencies:** `Skills/criticmarkup-editing.md` (delivery format); reference newsletters in `APR/Efforts/Newsletter/` optional for calibration; cross-platform emoji policy in `_social-posting-conventions.md` (agile-pain-relief-astro repo)

### APR Blog Critique
**Purpose:** Critiques a draft blog post against Mark's established writing style. Flags tone slips, off-voice vocabulary, and clunky sentence structures, plus a logic and content gap analysis and a dependency-order (information-DAG) check that section order grounds each term/concept before a later section leans on it. No rewrites. When the draft is a Markdown file, delivers the critique as inline CriticMarkup (see criticmarkup-editing); chat bullets are the fallback for pasted text.
**Triggers:** "critique this blog post," "review my blog draft," "blog critique," "voice check my blog," "does this blog sound like me"
**File:** `Skills/apr-blog-critique.md`
**Dependencies:** `Skills/criticmarkup-editing.md` (delivery format)

### CriticMarkup Editing
**Purpose:** Default delivery format for feedback on Mark's Markdown writing -- annotate the file in place with CriticMarkup (comments `{>>Claude: …<<}`, additions `{++…++}`, deletions `{--…--}`, substitutions `{~~old~>new~~}`, highlights `{==…==}`), reviewed in Obsidian's Track Changes side panel. The voice rubrics decide WHAT to flag; this skill decides HOW to deliver it. Always delivers the full markup pass in one go (no section-by-section chunking; the CLAUDE.md chunked-review preference does not apply to CriticMarkup passes). Applies to all writing types including sales/marketing copy. Never rewrites Mark's prose outside a markup wrapper. Falls back to chat bullets for pasted (non-file) content.
**Triggers:** "edit this," "mark up my draft," "track changes," "use CriticMarkup," "suggest edits inline," "give me feedback on my writing"
**File:** `Skills/criticmarkup-editing.md`
**Dependencies:** Obsidian Track Changes plugin (`.obsidian/plugins/track-changes/`); read alongside the relevant voice rubric (apr-blog-critique, apr-newsletter-reviewer, apr-linkedin-style, Marketing/copy-editing, storybrand-messaging)

### APR SEO Audit
**Purpose:** Diagnose structural SEO issues on agilepainrelief.com. Five-section audit framework (Crawlability, Technical, On-Page, Content/E-E-A-T, Authority) tightened for an Astro content/blog site. Produces a prioritised findings report at `APR/Analytics/seo-audit-YYYY-MM-DD.md`. Findings only, no auto-fix.
**Triggers:** "audit my SEO," "SEO audit," "why am I not ranking," "SEO health check," "my traffic dropped," "check my technical SEO"
**File:** `Skills/apr-seo-audit.md`
**Dependencies:** Bash access to the Astro repo, latest GSC export (run the `Google Search Console Export` task in Operations first if stale), browser for PSI / Rich Results Test

### Gmail Triage
**Purpose:** Recommend a triage plan for the Gmail inbox via the Gmail MCP. Classifies each thread into one of four actions — reference (file under existing label), reply-needed (draft suggestion only), trash, or archive (remove INBOX, keep in All Mail for records) — with a Task overlay for emails that imply an OmniFocus action. All recommendations require explicit per-item approval, presented in batches of 10. Replies handled in a separate pass. Only uses existing labels; never creates new ones. Trashing uses the Gmail TRASH label (30-day recovery). Sender-specific rules and aging rules live in `memory/feedback_gmail_triage.md`. Task captures delegate to `omnifocus-capture`.
**Triggers:** "triage my Gmail," "process my Gmail inbox," "Gmail triage," "sort my Gmail," "Gmail inbox zero"
**File:** `Skills/gmail-triage.md`
**Dependencies:** Gmail MCP connector (authenticated), `Skills/omnifocus-capture.md` (for Task overlay), `memory/feedback_gmail_triage.md` (sender rules)

### GrowthMaterial Export
**Purpose:** Export emails labelled `Courses and Memberships/GrowthMaterial` to Markdown under `~/Library/CloudStorage/Dropbox/3 - YFL/14 - TRAININGS & BIZ DEV/GrowthInReverse/Emails/`. Resumable across sessions via `_processed.json` state. Strips newsletter chrome (footer, tracking pixels, layout tables), downloads inline images locally to `images/`, names files `YYYY-MM-DD-sender-subject-slug.md` with YAML frontmatter. Skips Mark's own SENT forwards inside threads and the mis-labelled Scrum forum thread. Heavy lifting done by `_export.py` next to the output folder; Claude orchestrates one thread at a time to manage context burn from inline MCP returns. Optional duplicate detection pass at the end compares each new file against the sibling course-content folders (Growth/Monetization/Retention/Subscriber-Onboarding) and presents candidates for approval before deletion.
**Triggers:** "export GrowthMaterial emails," "update GrowthInReverse emails," "fetch new growth emails," "sync GrowthMaterial folder"
**File:** `Skills/growthmaterial-export.md`
**Dependencies:** Gmail MCP connector (authenticated), Python venv at `~/.local/share/growthmaterial-export/venv` (beautifulsoup4, markdownify, requests), conversion script at `<output>/_export.py`

### DevonThink Research
**Purpose:** Search, explore, and research across Mark's DevonThink library. Four modes - Miyo semantic search (default for conceptual queries; RAG over file body), DevonThink keyword search (precision filters by tag/author/kind/date), find-similar (by UUID or text passage), and AI-assisted research_topic (fans out across DevonThink + web + Wikipedia + arXiv + PubMed). Read-only; never writes back to DevonThink. Defaults to the `1. APR Research` database, collapses PDF/EPUB pairs, surfaces `x-devonthink-item://` links plus DOIs. Documents the library's folder ontology (Papers, Web Clippings, eBooks, Oxford Review, Course Materials) so results are labelled by source type. Miyo paths are resolved back to DevonThink UUIDs via `name:` field lookup (preserves colons and other macOS-illegal characters that `filename:` lookup misses) with a bare-term fallback.
**Triggers:** "search DevonThink," "find papers in DevonThink," "what do I have on [topic]," "semantic search [topic]," "DevonThink research," "similar in DevonThink"
**File:** `Skills/devonthink-research.md`
**Dependencies:** `miyo` MCP server (semantic search), `devonthink` MCP server (keyword/find-similar/research_topic/metadata), DevonThink app running

---

## Readwise Skills

Installed from https://github.com/readwiseio/readwise-skills. Each skill lives in its own subfolder under `Skills/Readwise/` with a `SKILL.md` file. These skills work against your Readwise + Reader library via the Readwise MCP server (https://mcp2.readwise.io/mcp) or the Readwise CLI. The `readwise-cli` and `readwise-mcp` skills are reference docs used by the other Readwise skills (similar to `omnifocus-workflow.md`).

### Readwise Triage
**Purpose:** Triage your Reader inbox one document at a time with a personalized pitch per item.
**Triggers:** "triage my Reader inbox," "process Reader inbox," "Reader inbox triage"
**File:** `Skills/Readwise/triage/SKILL.md`

# Weekly Review

Step back, look at the week, and plan the next one.

## When to Use

Run this once a week — Sunday evening, Monday morning, or whenever works for your rhythm.

## Instructions

### Step 1 - Gather
1. Check this week's calendar events (if calendar MCP is connected).
2. Review completed tasks or projects from the week.
3. Scan any notes, journal entries, or captured items from the past seven days.
4. **Email digest via the Gmail MCP** (see `Skills/gmail-triage.md` for conventions). Report counts per category - don't list individual emails unless Mark asks. Use `search_threads`:

   - Notifications unread (7d): `is:unread in:inbox category:updates newer_than:7d`

   (Meeting-transcript listing retired with Spark; there is no Gmail equivalent.)

6. **Writing Kanban review.** Open the APR Kanban view mentally - ask Mark which items he wants to commit to this week. Convert commitments into OmniFocus tasks via `omnifocus-capture`. The Kanban stays as idea pool + writing-capture; the weekly picks go to OmniFocus.
7. **Marketing Experiments check.** Skim `APR/Analytics/Experiments/_Experiments Index.md` for active experiments. Flag any whose monitoring dates have arrived.
8. **Repo work recap (what shipped).** Read-only git history across Mark's APR repos to summarize the week's shipped work. Repos:
   - APR astro (website): `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/agile-pain-relief-astro` (usually the bulk of the work; descriptive commit messages)
   - social-media-posting: `/Users/marklevison/Documents/GitHub/APR/social-media-posting` (evergreen/batch posting tooling; low volume)

   **Excluded - LifeHQ-Mark** (`/Users/marklevison/Documents/Obsidian/LifeHQ-Mark`): a global deny rule blocks Read/Edit/Write on it (set in `~/.claude/settings.json`), and it is all "Autocommit" vault backups anyway. Do not try to read it. If Mark asks why it is missing, point at the deny rule.

   For each repo, run (use `git -C <path>`, not `cd` - `cd` resets the shell cwd and can trip a permission prompt):
   ```bash
   # Commit list with messages
   git -C <repo> log --since="<start> 00:00" --date=short --pretty=format:"%ad | %s"
   # Per-commit scope, for sizing the work
   git -C <repo> log --since="<start> 00:00" --pretty=format:"%h %s" --shortstat
   # Area churn (which folders moved the most)
   git -C <repo> log --since="<start> 00:00" --pretty=format: --name-only \
     | grep -v '^$' | sed 's:/[^/]*$::' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -30
   ```
   Default window is the last 7 days (today minus 7); honor an explicit range if Mark gives one. Then:
   - Group commits into 2-5 themes per repo (e.g. email/CRM, funnel/quiz, sales pages, analytics refresh, course logistics). Lead with outcomes, not commit subjects.
   - Flag big diffs that are data churn (analytics dumps, generated PDFs, dependency removals) so they do not read as feature work - e.g. a "delete Drip" commit removing ~15,800 lines is cleanup, not net-new build.
   - Do not dump raw commits unless Mark asks; fold the recap into the "Shipped This Week" output section.
9. **OmniFocus inbox sweep.** Run `omnifocus-inbox-triage` to clear the OmniFocus inbox — walk each item, propose a project (plus tags/due/flag as needed), and apply approved edits as a batch. See `Skills/omnifocus-inbox-triage.md`. Skip if the inbox is empty; note the count either way.

11. **Content Ideas resurfacing.** Read `APR/Efforts/Content Ideas.md` and surface 2-3 hooks for Mark to consider promoting into Writing Tasks (`APR/TaskNotes/Tasks/`) or this week's plan. Rotate which ones you highlight so the whole list stays in view over time. Skip if the note is empty or missing.

### Step 2 — Review
1. Summarize what happened this week: key events, completed work, progress made.
2. Identify what's still open: tasks that didn't get finished, items that slipped.
3. Flag anything overdue or time-sensitive.

### Step 3 — Output
Produce a formatted weekly summary **in chat only**. This is an in-the-moment review — do not save it to a file, and do not ask reflective questions.

**Weekly Review — [Date Range]**

**What Happened**
[Key events, accomplishments, completed work.]

**Shipped This Week (Repos)**
[Per-repo themed bullets from the git recap, busiest repo first. One net line per repo (files, insertions, deletions) where it helps. Skip a repo with no commits in the window but say so in one line. LifeHQ-Mark excluded.]

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filt… [truncated]

# Content Ideas

Running list of quick hooks and angles for blog, newsletter, and social. Captured from the Drafts inbox triage. Review periodically and promote the good ones into Writing Tasks (`APR/TaskNotes/Tasks/`).

## Hooks

- **If we implemented every feature in your product backlog today, would your users be happy?** A provocative backlog-as-value question. (captured 2026-06-11)
- **BDD was always about the collaboration.** If you just use Given / When / Then to feed an LLM, it's a prompt with pretty formatting. (BDD + GenAI angle, captured 2026-06-04)
- **GenAI handles computer tasks fine; the more a question touches the real world or human emotions, the less reliable it gets.** (GenAI reliability angle, captured 2026-07-05)
- **Maximizing token budget is silly, going faster doesn't make you more productive.** (AI productivity angle, captured 2026-07-05)

# Marketing Experiments Index

One note per experiment. Each active experiment also has a single matching task in the `APR Business Owner > Marketing Experiments` project (single-actions list). The task note links back to the vault note via `obsidian://` URL; the vault note is the source of truth for goal, baseline, result, and learning.

**Review after:** All currently-active experiments are flagged for review after **2026-05-18** (see `review_after` in each note's frontmatter). Don't act on them before that date.

## Active / In Progress

### Newsletter experiments

- [[Embedded Long-Form Newsletter Content 2026-02-16]] — redefined 2026-06-14, status Not run (embed a full ~2,000-word blog post in the body)
- [[Question-Format Subject Lines 2026-02-16]]

### Social experiments

- [[Weekly Social Posting Schedule 2026-05-31]] — In progress but **not yet measurable** (no baseline; signup/course attribution absent from analytics). Review deferred to 2026-09-01.

### SEO / Content strategy (umbrella: [[Internal Linking and Content Cluster Strategy 2026-02-12]])

- [[GenAI Topic Cluster Build-Out 2026-02-12]]
- [[Declining Blog Post Refresh Batch 2026-02-12]]
- [[Pillar Page Creation 2026-02-12]] — blocked on GenAI cluster density
- [[In-Content Course Linking 2026-02-12]]
- [[Cluster 1 Metrics and Resilience Links 2026-06-16]] — cross-linking executed 2026-06-16, measure after 2026-08-11

## Complete — Succeeded

- [[Daily Scrum Guide Rework 2026-02-12]] — measured 2026-06-29: position 42.1 → 14.02 (beat the 15-20 target), impressions +38%; clicks still flat at page-2 position. Rewrite-for-ranking confirmed.
- [[Orphan Post Cleanup 2026-02-12]] — measured 2026-06-29: orphan count 73 → 24, all 19 targeted orphans now linked; GSC lift real on marquee pages (Spotify, AI cluster). Ongoing prevention is now monthly maintenance.
- [[Social Media GenAI Content Focus 2026-01-07]] — GenAI is now the primary content pillar
- [[LinkedIn Cadence 2025-11-24]] — Established weekday cadence baseline
- [[Drop Glossary Links from Newsletters 2026-02-16]] — Removing glossary links cost nothing; CTR held, space freed for blog/event CTAs

## Complete — Failed

- [[AI Failure Modes Quiz 2026-05-29]] — Failed across every channel (social, on-site quiz, on-site direct download); the theme, not the format, doesn't convert
- [[Lead Magnet Split Test Quiz vs eBook 2026-05-31]] — Quiz vs eBook made no difference; both null on tiny volume. Same verdict as the quiz overall
- [[Follow Me on Mastodon Newsletter Section 2026-02-16]] — Lifted profile clicks but produced no new followers
- [[Website CTA Banners to Webinar 2026-01-07]]
- [[Website CTA Banners to Agile Checkup 2025-11-21]]
- [[ScoreApp Quiz 2025-11-21]]
- [[Buffer Posting Schedule 2025-10-29]]

## Complete — Inconclusive

- [[Website Popup Banner A-B Variants 2026-01-19]]
- [[Main Menubar Redesign 2026-01-20]]
- [[Homepage Subscribe Form Copy 2025-11-05]]

## Conventions

- **Naming:** `<Experiment Name> YYYY-MM-DD.md` where the date is the start date
- **Frontmatter status values:** `In progress` | `Pending` | `Not run` | `Succeeded` | `Failed` | `Inconclusive`
- **`review_after` field:** ISO date. Skip this experiment's review until on or after this date.
- **OmniFocus pattern (revised 2026-06-16):** each active experiment is a parent task in the `APR Business Owner > Marketing Experiments` project (single-actions list, weekly review), sequential with two subtasks — `Execute:` (the work) and `Measure:` (blocked until Execute is done; its due date is set at the measurement window once Execute completes). Parent note carries a one-line goal/next-action plus an `obsidian://` link to this vault note. No due date on the parent or Execute. Flag the parent during Sunday review when it needs attention. Full pattern in `Skills/omnifocus-workflow.md`.

## Note from analytics

Analytics data does not currently include the number of students registered in courses or revenue numbers — factor that in when interpreting experiment outcomes.

## Related research

- [[State of the LinkedIn Algorithm Q1 2026 - Report and Call Notes]] - external LinkedIn algorithm report (Saywhat / Creator Accelerator) plus Mike Schmitz's commentary. Candidate experiments it suggests, not yet created: links-in-post vs link-in-comments, a Buffer cadence reset (3x/day toward quality), a visual-lane test (sketchnote / stick figure), and a Claude Skill lead magnet.

# OmniFocus Inbox Triage

Work through every item currently in the OmniFocus inbox. Per item, suggest a destination project plus optional edits. Apply approved changes in one batch.

## Before running

Read `Skills/omnifocus-workflow.md` for bucket mapping, tag semantics, and safety rails.

## MCP tools used

- `mcp__omnifocus__get_tasks` (inbox fetch)
- `mcp__omnifocus__get_projects` (destination options)
- `mcp__omnifocus__update_tasks` (batch apply)

## Instructions

### Step 1, load context

Call in parallel:

- `get_tasks(inbox_only=true)` to list what's in the inbox
- `get_projects()` to have the full destination list

### Step 2, propose a triage plan

For each inbox task, suggest:

- **Destination project** (must exist; no guessing)
- **Rename** (only when the current name is unclear)
- **Due date** (only when context strongly implies one)
- **Flag** (only when clearly urgent)
- **Tags** (only when obvious; see workflow doc tag section)

Present as a table:

| ID | Current Name | Project | Rename | Due | Flag | Tags |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| abcd1234 | buy milk | Household | (keep) | (none) | no | Errands |
| efgh5678 | look into pricing | Business Evolution | Review Effective Scrum pricing tiers | 2026-04-30 | yes | (none) |
| ijkl9012 | random idea | **needs new project** | (discuss) | | | |

If nothing in the project tree fits, flag as "needs new project" and leave the task in the inbox.

### Step 3, wait for approval

Ask Mark:

- Accept the full plan?
- Cherry-pick (accept some, skip others)?
- Adjust a specific row?

Do **not** execute until Mark says go.

### Step 4, execute as one batch

Collect all approved rows and call `update_tasks` once with an array. This is efficient and atomic-feeling.

Example shape:
```json
{
  "tasks": [
    {"id": "abcd1234", "project_id": "<Household id>", "tags": ["Errands"]},
    {"id": "efgh5678", "project_id": "<Business Evolution id>", "name": "Review Effective Scrum pricing tiers", "due_date": "2026-04-30", "flagged": true}
  ]
}
```

### Step 5, report

> Triaged 7 of 9 inbox items. 2 flagged as "needs new project" and left in the inbox.
>
> - Household: Buy milk, Pick up dry cleaning
> - Business Evolution: Review Effective Scrum pricing tiers (renamed, flagged, due 2026-04-30)
> - ...

## Rules

- **Never guess a project.** If nothing fits, leave the task in the inbox and note "needs new project."
- **Preserve user intent.** Only rename when the original is unclear. Don't tidy for the sake of tidying.
- **Never delete or drop.** Triage moves tasks, it doesn't kill them.
- **Honor cherry-picks.** Execute only approved rows.
- **Ambiguous project names:** if a name appears in multiple folders, stop and ask.
- **Batch confirmation is required.** Triage is always a batch operation.

---

*Part of the OmniFocus skill family. Shared conventions live in `Skills/omnifocus-workflow.md`.*
