5	
6	# OmniFocus Workflow with Cowork
7	
8	This doc is the shared context the OmniFocus skills need to behave like Mark expects. The skill files themselves focus on *how to call the MCP*; this doc captures *Mark's conventions*.
9	
10	**Skills that read this:** `omnifocus-capture`, `omnifocus-query`, `omnifocus-inbox-triage`, `omnifocus-focus`.
11	
12	Mark drives weekly / project reviews directly in the OmniFocus app, not through a skill. The cadence data below is reference only.
13	
14	---
15	
16	## 1. The Three Buckets
17	
18	Mark organizes work into three buckets. These map cleanly onto existing OmniFocus folders.
19	
20	| Bucket | Folders | Projects |
21	|---|---|---|
22	| **Personal/Family** | Family, Me, Learner and Explorer | Household, Husband, Father, Me, Friendship, Important Reading Queue, Photography, Experiments |
23	| **APR** (Agile Pain Relief) | APR Business Owner | Initiatives (folder: per-outcome projects), Operations, Ideas & Reading, Marketing Experiments |
24	| **YFL** (Your Financial Launchpad) | YFL CTO | YFL Other |
25	
26	**Notes:**
27	- Personal/Family spans three folders but is one bucket for routing purposes.
28	- YFL is early-stage (only one project at time of writing). Expect this to grow.
29	- When a skill talks about "bucket," it means one of these three. Use folder membership to determine bucket.
30	
31	### Bucket routing notes (confirmed 2026-04-19)
32	
33	- **Programming was removed 2026-04-20.** Contents migrated to Experiments. Project status = dropped (kept for history). Do not route anything to Programming.
34	- **Experiments is the broad catch-all** in the Learner and Explorer folder. It absorbs: actual software development work, automation, tool tweaks, Obsidian setup and customization, Keyboard Maestro / Alfred / iOS Shortcuts tweaks, dashboard building, tool-of-the-week experiments, PKM methodology trials.
35	- **"Learner and Experimentation" is Mark's shorthand for the Experiments project.** Treat the phrase as a direct reference to that project, not the folder.
36	- **Important Reading Queue (Me):** dual-purpose. May contain both personal and business-oriented reading. Route to the project when named, never assume bucket.
37	- **Reading vs. practicing a technique:** if the task is "read about X," it goes to Important Reading Queue. If the task is "try X in my own life or work," it usually belongs in Experiments (personal) or the relevant APR project (business).
38	- **YFL:** this is Mark's wife's business. Low volume. Unlikely to need sub-folders soon. Keep the one-folder pattern.
39	
40	### APR mode-based structure (added 2026-05-31)
41	
42	APR Business Owner is organised by **mode**, not subject area. Four buckets:
43	
44	- **Initiatives** (folder, one project per outcome) — committed multi-step work with real dependencies. Examples currently active: `GenAI Cohort Launch`, `Drip → Cakemail Cleanup`, `Vendor & Tool Migrations`, `A-CSM Relaunch`. When Mark says "I'm starting X" or commits to a launch, capture as a new project here. Drop the project when the outcome ships.
45	- **Operations** (single-actions, weekly review) — recurring admin and meta-tasks: bills, licence renewals, weekly analytics pull, monthly GSC export, bi-weekly blog refresh, etc. Anything that repeats on a cadence lives here.
46	- **Ideas & Reading** (single-actions, monthly review) — parking lot for curiosities, reading material, "consider X," "look into Y." Tagged by theme: `AI Exploration`, `Business Strategy`, `Tooling Curiosity`. Monthly review = scan, prune, promote 1-2 to Initiatives if Mark commits.
47	- **Marketing Experiments** (single-actions, weekly review) — one task per active experiment; see the Marketing Experiments pattern section below.
48	
49	**Replaces the old subject-area projects** (Business Evolution, Ongoing Business, Website, Pragmatic LLM Uses, Agile and AI) which were all dropped 2026-05-31. The old names became fuzzy idea-queues rather than coherent projects, which made review mechanical.
50	
51	**Routing rule for APR captures:**
52	- Committed multi-step outcome? → Initiatives (existing project, or new one if it's a new commitment — ask)
53	- Recurring admin or maintenance? → Operations
54	- Curiosity, idea, reading item? → Ideas & Reading (with the right theme tag)
55	- Marketing test with a measurement window? → Marketing Experiments (one new task; see below)
56	- If unclear, ask. Don't infer.
57	
58	### Routing patterns observed (from 2026-04-19 triage; APR rows updated 2026-05-31)
59	
60	These patterns emerged from the first batch triage session. Use them as defaults, not rigid rules. Always confirm when uncertain.
61	
62	| Capture shape | Usual destination |
63	|---|---|
64	| Obsidian plugin, dashboard, or vault setup tweak | Experiments |
65	| Alfred, Keyboard Maestro, iOS Shortcuts automation | Experiments |
66	| "Check out this new tool / app / workflow" (personal curiosity) | Experiments |
67	| Claude / MCP integration research for business use | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `AI Exploration` |
68	| AI tool Mark wants to evaluate for business use | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `AI Exploration` (or `Tooling Curiosity` if tooling-for-tooling) |
69	| YFL application work (Supabase, etc.) | YFL Other |
70	| Business file/vendor cleanup (recurring) | Operations (APR) |
71	| Business migration off a vendor (committed) | Initiatives > Vendor & Tool Migrations (APR) — or new Initiative project if scope warrants |
72	| Personal file/systems cleanup | Me |
73	| GenAI experiments tied to Scrum / Agile (idea or reading) | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `AI Exploration` |
74	| GenAI cohort launch work | Initiatives > GenAI Cohort Launch (APR) |
75	| Course prep / delivery / ops (recurring) | Operations (APR) |
76	| Course relaunch (committed initiative) | Initiatives > new project, e.g. A-CSM Relaunch (APR) |
77	| APR marketing content / keynote ideas | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `Business Strategy` (or `AI Exploration` if AI-focused) |
78	| APR strategic question or "should I X?" | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `Business Strategy` |
79	| Drip → Cakemail migration cleanup | Initiatives > Drip → Cakemail Cleanup (APR) |
80	| Recurring APR admin (bills, licence renewals, analytics pulls) | Operations (APR) |
81	| Marketing experiment (new test) | Marketing Experiments (APR) — one new task with vault note |
82	| Writing/glossary idea | `APR/TaskNotes/` in the vault (not OmniFocus). One file per idea, frontmatter: `tags: task`, `status: LongTerm`, `priority: normal`, `ContentType: [Blog \| Glossary \| Newsletter]`. Filename = the idea title. Body optional (URLs, context). Mark moves them to `APR/Efforts/Glossary/` or `APR/Efforts/Blog/` manually when the work begins. |
83	| Reading material (book, article, paper) | Important Reading Queue |
84	| Physical shopping or household purchases | Household |
85	| Camera or photography gear | Photography |
86	| Self-development practice (techniques to try in daily life) | Me or Experiments |
87	| Coaching / questioning techniques | Experiments (as practice material) |
88	
89	**Mark's colloquial project names vs. where they now go (updated 2026-05-31):**
90	
91	| Mark says | Where it goes |
92	|---|---|
93	| "APR Business" | Depends on shape — recurring admin → Operations; strategic idea/question → Ideas & Reading (Business Strategy tag); committed launch → Initiatives (new or existing project). Ask which. |
94	| "Learner and Experimentation" | Experiments (personal, Learner and Explorer folder) |
95	| "Agile AI" / "Agile and AI" | Ideas & Reading + AI Exploration tag; or GenAI Cohort Launch if it's clearly cohort work |
96	| "Pragmatic LLM usage" | Ideas & Reading + AI Exploration tag |
97	| "Marketing experiment" / "new experiment" | Marketing Experiments — one new task with rich note + vault link |
98	| "I'm starting [X]" / "new initiative" | New project in Initiatives folder |
99	| "Business Evolution" / "Ongoing Business" / "Website" / "Pragmatic LLM Uses" | These projects were dropped 2026-05-31. Route by mode (see above) instead. |
100	
101	### Marketing Experiments pattern (APR) — restructured 2026-06-16
102	
103	Marketing Experiments are tracked in two linked places:
104	
105	- **Vault note per experiment** in `APR/Analytics/Experiments/` — holds the Goal, Baseline, What Changed, Result, Learning narrative. Index at `APR/Analytics/Experiments/_Experiments Index.md`.
106	- **One parent task per experiment** inside the single `Marketing Experiments` project under `APR Business Owner` (project type = single-actions list, weekly review). The parent name + note carry just enough context to act; the vault note holds the depth.
107	
108	**Why this shape (not project-per-experiment):** experiments aren't multi-step projects — they're "make a change, wait, check results." A project wrapper per experiment caused review blur (near-identical mini-projects all looking the same in review). One parent task per experiment keeps the whole portfolio visible at a glance.
109	
110	**The Do → Measure structure (added 2026-06-16):** an experiment has two phases that must not be conflated — *doing the work* and *measuring the result later*. Each parent task is **sequential** with exactly two subtasks:
111	
112	- **`Execute: <action>`** — the change/work. Pull-based, no due date.
113	- **`Measure: <metric>`** — blocked until Execute is complete. **Set its due date only when Execute is checked off**, at the measurement window (below). This is the mechanism that stops "remember to go get the data" from quietly evaporating once the work is done.
114	
115	When the work was finished before this structure existed, create the Execute subtask already-completed and set the Measure due date immediately.
116	
117	**Measurement window defaults (SEO/content experiments):**
118	
119	- **Linking or refresh of existing pages → ~8 weeks** after the work ships (re-crawl + re-rank of pages Google already knows).
120	- **New posts / pillar pages → ~12 weeks** (new URLs need indexation time before they accrue enough impressions to read).
121	- In practice, measure at the **next monthly GSC refresh on or after** that mark. Non-SEO experiments (newsletter, lead-magnet) use the window named in their own vault note.
122	
123	**Task conventions:**
124	
125	- **Parent name:** experiment name without the date suffix, e.g. `Question-Format Subject Lines`.
126	- **Parent note:** one line of context (goal / next action), then a blank line, then the `obsidian://open?vault=MarkPKM&file=...` link to the vault note (URL-encode spaces as `%20`, slashes as `%2F`). Keep the depth in the vault note, not here.
127	- **No due date on the parent or the Execute subtask.** Only the Measure subtask carries a due date, and only once Execute is done.
128	- **No tags by default.** Flag the parent at review time if the experiment is the focus of the week (`Weekly Plan` tag is the equivalent signal).
129	
130	**Weekly review mechanism:** during Sunday review, open the `Marketing Experiments` project and **flag 1-2 parents** to surface them for the week. Measure subtasks with a due date surface on their own.
131	
132	**Completion:** when the Measure subtask is done, mark the parent complete and update the vault note's `Result` and `Learning` sections.
133	
134	**Triggering:** when Mark says "new marketing experiment [name]", capture a **new parent task** (with the Execute → Measure subtasks) in the `Marketing Experiments` project — not a new project, not a new folder — and ask whether the vault note already exists or needs to be created.
135	
136	### Triage-specific rules learned
137	
138	- **Already-done items:** during triage, Mark sometimes reveals an inbox item is already complete. Mark it completed (`completed: true`) instead of moving it. Easier than a move-then-complete.
139	- **Ghost inbox items:** the inbox will contain some items with `status: dropped` that never fully cleared. Flag them to Mark but leave them alone. Cleanup happens in the OmniFocus app.
140	- **Tags during triage:** Mark occasionally tags at triage time (for example, `Weekly Plan` on items that belong in a weekly planning view). Triage skill supports `add_tags` per item, use it.
141	- **"Skip" means leave in inbox.** Don't drop, don't defer, just leave the item where it is so Mark can handle it manually.
142	
143	---
144	
145	## 2. Capture Conventions
146	
147	- **Default destination: inbox.** Always, unless Mark explicitly names a project in the ask.
148	- Example triggers that still go to inbox: "add a task to call Sam", "drop this in OmniFocus"
149	- Example trigger that goes to a project: "add 'refactor login flow' to Website"
150	- Single captures proceed without confirmation.
151	- Batch captures (more than one task) get a confirmation step.
152	- Never infer a project from context. If Mark's wording is ambiguous, ask.
153	
154	---
155	
156	## 3. Roles and the Status-Tag Pull System (restructured 2026-06-14)
157	
158	Mark runs a roles-pull system adapted from MacSparky's Roles workshop. Roles set the "what am I working on" axis; status tags set the Kanban lane. Tasks are "endeavours" in that language. This replaces the old flat planning/state tag scheme (the previous Bench / Consider Next / Quarterly Plan setup).
159	
160	### Roles = folders
161	
162	The three in-scope roles map one to one onto OmniFocus folders. Folder membership *is* the role, so there are no role tags.
163	
164	| Role | Folder |
165	|---|---|
166	| Learner and Explorer | Learner and Explorer |
167	| APR Business Owner | APR Business Owner |
168	| YFL CTO | YFL CTO |
169	
170	Family and Me are parked (not yet rolled in). Arete statements for each role live in [Self/Roles.md](../Self/Roles.md). They are the values filter for deciding what is worth pulling onto a given week.
171	
172	### Status tags (the Kanban lanes)
173	
174	| Tag | Meaning |
175	|---|---|
176	| *(untagged)* | **Idea / backlog.** The default. Anything without a status tag is an idea, not a commitment. |
177	| `Shelf` | Warm queue. On-deck, coming back soon. |
178	| `Next Week` | Committed for next week. The staging lane. |
179	| `Weekly Plan` | Committed for this week. The week's pool. |
180	| `Doing` | In progress right now. The active lane, and where the tight WIP limit lives. |
181	| `Waiting` | Blocked on someone else. A separate axis, not part of the pull flow. |
182	
183	No `Done` tag. Completing the task in OmniFocus *is* done. Add one only if a draggable "done" board column is ever wanted.
184	
185	### The pull flow
186	
187	Backlog (untagged) to `Shelf` to `Next Week` to `Weekly Plan` to `Doing` to completed.
188	
189	- **WIP limits.** The tight, meaningful limit lives on `Doing`, the active lane (start around 1 to 3). `Weekly Plan` carries a looser weekly commitment cap (around 5 to 7). Both apply only to discretionary endeavour work; Mark sets the numbers.
190	- **Pull into `Doing` as you start.** Day to day, move an item from `Weekly Plan` to `Doing` when you actually begin it, and out again when you stop or complete it. `Doing` is the honest "what am I touching right now" lane.
191	- **Recurring Operations tasks carry no status tag.** Analytics pulls, GSC export, blog refresh, and the like flow on their own recurrence plus due dates and never count against the WIP limit. They are maintenance throughput, not pulled endeavours.
192	- **Mid-week arrivals destined for next week get `Next Week`, never `Weekly Plan`.** This keeps the current week's board stable once it is set; the item joins this week only when Sunday promotes it.
193	- `Weekly Plan` is the canonical "this week" signal across all folders. Where the Marketing Experiments pattern (Section 1) says "flag to surface for the week," the `Weekly Plan` tag is the equivalent; flagging stays a compatible secondary highlight.
194	
195	### The Sunday pull (weekly review event, done in the OmniFocus app)
196	
197	1. Complete or clear what finished.
198	2. Promote `Next Week` into `Weekly Plan`.
199	3. Refill `Next Week` and `Shelf` from the backlog, up to the WIP limit.
200	4. Glance at the role mix: is any role starving?
201	
202	The review is the forcing function. It is what keeps the backlog from breeding zombies (the old `Quarterly Plan` problem): quarter candidates simply sit as backlog or `Shelf` and get pulled forward when they are actually due, instead of wearing a sticky tag that never expires.
203	
204	### Tag migration (applied 2026-06-14; supersedes the 2026-04-19 cleanup plan)
205	
206	Done in OmniFocus on 2026-06-14:
207	
208	- **Added:** `Shelf`, `Next Week`.
209	- **Kept:** `Weekly Plan` (now the WIP lane), `Waiting` (unchanged: blocked on someone else).
210	- **Folded into `Shelf`:** the 11 live tasks carrying `Consider Next` were re-tagged to `Shelf`; `Bench` had no tasks. Both tags set to `dropped`. `Bench` is retired because its old meaning ("paused") is the opposite of MacSparky's bench ("active this week").
211	- **Retired quarter tags:** `Quarterly Plan` and `Q2 2026` set to `dropped` and stripped from their 13 live tasks (which fall back to untagged backlog); the older quarter tags (`Q1`-`Q4 2025`, `Q3`/`Q4 2024`) were already dropped.
212	- Dropped tags are hidden, not hard-deleted, so they are recoverable; hard-delete in the app if wanted.
213	- 8 tasks in dropped/dead projects still carry the now-hidden old tags; left untouched per the ghost-item rule.
214	
215	### Other existing tags (unchanged by this change)
216	
217	- **Ideas & Reading themes:** `AI Exploration`, `Business Strategy`, `Tooling Curiosity`. Tag tasks inside the `Ideas & Reading` project (APR) to filter the parking lot by theme during monthly review.
218	- **GTD contexts:** `Phone Calls`, `Errands`, `Home`, `Office`, `Online`, `Communications`.
219	- **Recurrence cadence:** `Daily`, `Weekly`, `Monthly`, `Quarterly`, `SemiAnnually`, `Annually`.
220	- **Domain / utility:** `Health`, `Writing`, `Glossary`, `Checklist`, `Automate`. People / scope: `Family`, `Friends`. (The old `Heatlh` typo is already fixed.)
221	- **Leftover:** the `!Plan` grouping tag is still active but unused by this scheme; retire it whenever convenient.
222	
223	---
224	
225	## 4. Review Cadence (observed)
226	
227	Pulled from project `reviewIntervalValue` / `reviewIntervalUnit` on 2026-04-19:
228	
229	| Project | Folder | Interval |
230	|---|---|---|
231	| Me | Me | Every 4 days |
232	| Household | Family | Every 2 weeks |
233	| Husband | Family | Every 9 days |
234	| Father | Family | Every 23 days |
235	| Friendship | Me | Every 10 days |
236	| Important Reading Queue | Me | Weekly |
237	| Photography | Learner and Explorer | Every 2 weeks |
238	| Experiments | Learner and Explorer | Every 16 days |
239	| GenAI Cohort Launch | APR > Initiatives | Weekly |
240	| Drip → Cakemail Cleanup | APR > Initiatives | Every 2 weeks |
241	| Vendor & Tool Migrations | APR > Initiatives | Monthly |
242	| A-CSM Relaunch | APR > Initiatives | Every 2 weeks |
243	| Operations | APR | Weekly |
244	| Ideas & Reading | APR | Monthly |
245	| Marketing Experiments | APR | Weekly |
246	| YFL Other | YFL CTO | Every 23 days |
247	
248	**Cadence pattern:** APR Initiatives + Operations + Marketing Experiments review weekly to bi-weekly; Ideas & Reading reviews monthly (it's a parking lot, not a commitment list). Personal/Family varies. Old subject-area APR projects (Business Evolution, Website, Ongoing Business, Pragmatic LLM Uses, Agile and AI, Ship30For30) all dropped 2026-05-31 in the mode-based restructure.
249	
250	**Review is done in the OmniFocus app**, not via a skill. Skills may surface review-adjacent info when asked (e.g. "what's stalled") via `omnifocus-query`.
251	
252	---
253	
254	## 5. Focus / Perspective Use
255	
256	### Confirmed 2026-04-19
257	
258	- Mark uses two custom perspectives: **Weekly Plan** and **Quarterly Plan**. Both are general (not bucket-specific) and rarely used.
259	- **Focus is a nice-to-have, not a daily habit yet.** The `omnifocus-focus` skill ships minimal: set focus on a bucket folder, clear focus, show current focus. No perspective switching wired in yet.
260	- **Bucket to folder mapping for focus:**
261	    - "Focus on APR" → set focus on `APR Business Owner` folder
262	    - "Focus on YFL" → set focus on `YFL CTO` folder
263	    - "Focus on Personal/Family" → spans three folders (`Family`, `Me`, `Learner and Explorer`). The skill should ask which specific folder, or apply all three if the MCP supports multi-folder focus.
264	    - "Clear focus" → reset
265	
266	Revisit perspective integration once Mark actually starts using focus regularly.
267	
268	### Kanban status board (added 2026-06-14)
269	
270	The status tags from Section 3 (`Shelf`, `Next Week`, `Weekly Plan`, `Doing`) are designed to drive a custom perspective grouped by tag. That grouping is the Kanban board, one column per lane. Filter it to a single folder for a one-role board, or leave it across all three folders for the whole picture. OmniFocus 4 has no native board view, so tag-grouping is the approximation. Repoint the existing "Weekly Plan" perspective at this scheme; the "Quarterly Plan" perspective can be retired along with the quarter tags.
271	
272	---
273	
274	## 6. Recurrence (repeating tasks and projects)
275	
276	The MCP supports recurrence on both tasks and projects. Use `create_tasks` / `create_projects` to seed the task, then apply recurrence via `update_tasks` / `update_projects` (the create calls don't take recurrence fields directly as of 2026-04-20).
277	
278	### Fields
279	
280	- `recurrence` — an iCalendar RRULE string, or `""` to clear recurrence.
281	- `repetition_method` — how the next occurrence is scheduled:
282	    - `fixed` — next occurrence is calculated from the *original* schedule, regardless of when it's completed. Best for rhythms that should happen on a consistent day (weekly review, monthly bills).
283	    - `start_after_completion` — next defer date is X after you actually complete it. Best for tasks where the gap between completions matters more than the date (water the plants, lubricate the bike chain).
284	    - `due_after_completion` — next due date is X after you actually complete it. Similar to above but for due-dated tasks.
285	
286	### Common RRULEs
287	
288	| Cadence | RRULE |
289	|---|---|
290	| Every day | `FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=1` |
291	| Every weekday | `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR` |
292	| Weekly | `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1` |
293	| Every 2 weeks | `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2` |
294	| Monthly | `FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=1` |
295	| Quarterly | `FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=3` |
296	| Annually | `FREQ=YEARLY;INTERVAL=1` |
297	
298	### Default choices
299	
300	- **Rhythms (weekly review, analytics pull, reviews)** → `repetition_method: fixed` so the cadence stays consistent.
301	- **Maintenance tasks (chores, bike tune-up, HVAC filter)** → `repetition_method: start_after_completion` so the clock resets on completion.
302	- **Due-dated tasks (bill pay, quarterly filing)** → `repetition_method: due_after_completion`.
303	
304	### Reading recurrence from a task
305	
306	The `get_tasks` response includes `isRecurring`, `recurrence` (RRULE), `repetitionMethod`, and `repeatSummary` (human-readable, always prefer this for display). `nextDueDate` / `nextDeferDate` are populated for recurring tasks.
307	
308	### Safe update pattern
309	
310	```python
311	update_tasks(tasks=[{
312	    "id": task_id,
313	    "recurrence": "FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1",
314	    "repetition_method": "fixed"
315	}])
316	```
317	
318	Clearing recurrence: `recurrence: ""`.
319	
320	---
321	
322	## 7. Skill Safety Rails (applies to all)
323	
324	- **Reads:** no confirmation needed.
325	- **Single writes** (one task create, one task update): proceed immediately, report result.
326	- **Batch writes** (more than one task affected): show the plan, wait for approval.
327	- **Deletes:** always confirm. Prefer `drop` over `delete` unless Mark says "permanently delete."
328	- **Recurring task completion:** use the MCP's proper completion mechanism, never a raw "set completed to true" pattern. The MCP handles next-occurrence generation.
329	
330	---
331	
332	## 8. Cowork Bridge Notes
333	
334	- The OmniFocus MCP runs on Mark's Mac. From Cowork, the `mcp__omnifocus__*` tools call into it directly.
335	- If the MCP is disconnected, the skills can't run. Tell Mark to restart Claude Desktop / re-enable the MCP.
336	- Rich data is available via MCP; no need for pasted output or dump files.
337	
338	---
339	
340	*Last updated: 2026-06-16 (Marketing Experiments Do → Measure subtask structure + measurement-window defaults; Section 1). Update this doc whenever conventions change. The skills read it at runtime to stay aligned.*
341

---
name: omnifocus-workflow
description: Shared conventions, bucket mapping, and tag system for the OmniFocus skill family. Read this before running any OmniFocus skill.
---

# OmniFocus Workflow with Cowork

This doc is the shared context the OmniFocus skills need to behave like Mark expects. The skill files themselves focus on *how to call the MCP*; this doc captures *Mark's conventions*.

**Skills that read this:** `omnifocus-capture`, `omnifocus-query`, `omnifocus-inbox-triage`, `omnifocus-focus`.

Mark drives weekly / project reviews directly in the OmniFocus app, not through a skill. The cadence data below is reference only.

---

## 1. The Three Buckets

Mark organizes work into three buckets. These map cleanly onto existing OmniFocus folders.

| Bucket | Folders | Projects |
|---|---|---|
| **Personal/Family** | Family, Me, Learner and Explorer | Household, Husband, Father, Me, Friendship, Important Reading Queue, Photography, Experiments |
| **APR** (Agile Pain Relief) | APR Business Owner | Initiatives (folder: per-outcome projects), Operations, Ideas & Reading, Marketing Experiments |
| **YFL** (Your Financial Launchpad) | YFL CTO | YFL Other |

**Notes:**
- Personal/Family spans three folders but is one bucket for routing purposes.
- YFL is early-stage (only one project at time of writing). Expect this to grow.
- When a skill talks about "bucket," it means one of these three. Use folder membership to determine bucket.

### Bucket routing notes (confirmed 2026-04-19)

- **Programming was removed 2026-04-20.** Contents migrated to Experiments. Project status = dropped (kept for history). Do not route anything to Programming.
- **Experiments is the broad catch-all** in the Learner and Explorer folder. It absorbs: actual software development work, automation, tool tweaks, Obsidian setup and customization, Keyboard Maestro / Alfred / iOS Shortcuts tweaks, dashboard building, tool-of-the-week experiments, PKM methodology trials.
- **"Learner and Experimentation" is Mark's shorthand for the Experiments project.** Treat the phrase as a direct reference to that project, not the folder.
- **Important Reading Queue (Me):** dual-purpose. May contain both personal and business-oriented reading. Route to the project when named, never assume bucket.
- **Reading vs. practicing a technique:** if the task is "read about X," it goes to Important Reading Queue. If the task is "try X in my own life or work," it usually belongs in Experiments (personal) or the relevant APR project (business).
- **YFL:** this is Mark's wife's business. Low volume. Unlikely to need sub-folders soon. Keep the one-folder pattern.

### APR mode-based structure (added 2026-05-31)

APR Business Owner is organised by **mode**, not subject area. Four buckets:

- **Initiatives** (folder, one project per outcome) — committed multi-step work with real dependencies. Examples currently active: `GenAI Cohort Launch`, `Drip → Cakemail Cleanup`, `Vendor & Tool Migrations`, `A-CSM Relaunch`. When Mark says "I'm starting X" or commits to a launch, capture as a new project here. Drop the project when the outcome ships.
- **Operations** (single-actions, weekly review) — recurring admin and meta-tasks: bills, licence renewals, weekly analytics pull, monthly GSC export, bi-weekly blog refresh, etc. Anything that repeats on a cadence lives here.
- **Ideas & Reading** (single-actions, monthly review) — parking lot for curiosities, reading material, "consider X," "look into Y." Tagged by theme: `AI Exploration`, `Business Strategy`, `Tooling Curiosity`. Monthly review = scan, prune, promote 1-2 to Initiatives if Mark commits.
- **Marketing Experiments** (single-actions, weekly review) — one task per active experiment; see the Marketing Experiments pattern section below.

**Replaces the old subject-area projects** (Business Evolution, Ongoing Business, Website, Pragmatic LLM Uses, Agile and AI) which were all dropped 2026-05-31. The old names became fuzzy idea-queues rather than coherent projects, which made review mechanical.

**Routing rule for APR captures:**
- Committed multi-step outcome? → Initiatives (existing project, or new one if it's a new commitment — ask)
- Recurring admin or maintenance? → Operations
- Curiosity, idea, reading item? → Ideas & Reading (with the right theme tag)
- Marketing test with a measurement window? → Marketing Experiments (one new task; see below)
- If unclear, ask. Don't infer.

### Routing patterns observed (from 2026-04-19 triage; APR rows updated 2026-05-31)

These patterns emerged from the first batch triage session. Use them as defaults, not rigid rules. Always confirm when uncertain.

| Capture shape | Usual destination |
|---|---|
| Obsidian plugin, dashboard, or vault setup tweak | Experiments |
| Alfred, Keyboard Maestro, iOS Shortcuts automation | Experiments |
| "Check out this new tool / app / workflow" (personal curiosity) | Experiments |
| Claude / MCP integration research for business use | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `AI Exploration` |
| AI tool Mark wants to evaluate for business use | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `AI Exploration` (or `Tooling Curiosity` if tooling-for-tooling) |
| YFL application work (Supabase, etc.) | YFL Other |
| Business file/vendor cleanup (recurring) | Operations (APR) |
| Business migration off a vendor (committed) | Initiatives > Vendor & Tool Migrations (APR) — or new Initiative project if scope warrants |
| Personal file/systems cleanup | Me |
| GenAI experiments tied to Scrum / Agile (idea or reading) | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `AI Exploration` |
| GenAI cohort launch work | Initiatives > GenAI Cohort Launch (APR) |
| Course prep / delivery / ops (recurring) | Operations (APR) |
| Course relaunch (committed initiative) | Initiatives > new project, e.g. A-CSM Relaunch (APR) |
| APR marketing content / keynote ideas | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `Business Strategy` (or `AI Exploration` if AI-focused) |
| APR strategic question or "should I X?" | Ideas & Reading (APR) + tag `Business Strategy` |
| Drip → Cakemail migration cleanup | Initiatives > Drip → Cakemail Cleanup (APR) |
| Recurring APR admin (bills, licence renewals, analytics pulls) | Operations (APR) |
| Marketing experiment (new test) | Marketing Experiments (APR) — one new task with vault note |
| Writing/glossary idea | `APR/TaskNotes/` in the vault (not OmniFocus). One file per idea, frontmatter: `tags: task`, `status: LongTerm`, `priority: normal`, `ContentType: [Blog \| Glossary \| Newsletter]`. Filename = the idea title. Body optional (URLs, context). Mark moves them to `APR/Efforts/Glossary/` or `APR/Efforts/Blog/` manually when the work begins. |
| Reading material (book, article, paper) | Important Reading Queue |
| Physical shopping or household purchases | Household |
| Camera or photography gear | Photography |
| Self-development practice (techniques to try in daily life) | Me or Experiments |
| Coaching / questioning techniques | Experiments (as practice material) |

**Mark's colloquial project names vs. where they now go (updated 2026-05-31):**

| Mark says | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| "APR Business" | Depends on shape — recurring admin → Operations; strategic idea/question → Ideas & Reading (Business Strategy tag); committed launch → Initiatives (new or existing project). Ask which. |
| "Learner and Experimentation" | Experiments (personal, Learner and Explorer folder) |
| "Agile AI" / "Agile and AI" | Ideas & Reading + AI Exploration tag; or GenAI Cohort Launch if it's clearly cohort work |
| "Pragmatic LLM usage" | Ideas & Reading + AI Exploration tag |
| "Marketing experiment" / "new experiment" | Marketing Experiments — one new task with rich note + vault link |
| "I'm starting [X]" / "new initiative" | New project in Initiatives folder |
| "Business Evolution" / "Ongoing Business" / "Website" / "Pragmatic LLM Uses" | These projects were dropped 2026-05-31. Route by mode (see above) instead. |

### Marketing Experiments pattern (APR) — restructured 2026-06-16

Marketing Experiments are tracked in two linked places:

- **Vault note per experiment** in `APR/Analytics/Experiments/` — holds the Goal, Baseline, What Changed, Result, Learning narrative. Index at `APR/Analytics/Experiments/_Experiments Index.md`.
- **One parent task per experiment** inside the single `Marketing Experiments` project under `APR Business Owner` (project type = single-actions list, weekly review). The parent name + note carry just enough context to act; the vault note holds the depth.

**Why this shape (not project-per-experiment):** experiments aren't multi-step projects — they're "make a change, wait, check results." A project wrapper per experiment caused review blur (near-identical mini-projects all looking the same in review). One parent task per experiment keeps the whole portfolio visible at a glance.

**The Do → Measure structure (added 2026-06-16):** an experiment has two phases that must not be conflated — *doing the work* and *measuring the result later*. Each parent task is **sequential** with exactly two subtasks:

- **`Execute: <action>`** — the change/work. Pull-based, no due date.
- **`Measure: <metric>`** — blocked until Execute is complete. **Set its due date only when Execute is checked off**, at the measurement window (below). This is the mechanism that stops "remember to go get the data" from quietly evaporating once the work is done.

When the work was finished before this structure existed, create the Execute subtask already-completed and set the Measure due date immediately.

**Measurement window defaults (SEO/content experiments):**

- **Linking or refresh of existing pages → ~8 weeks** after the work ships (re-crawl + re-rank of pages Google already knows).
- **New posts / pillar pages → ~12 weeks** (new URLs need indexation time before they accrue enough impressions to read).
- In practice, measure at the **next monthly GSC refresh on or after** that mark. Non-SEO experiments (newsletter, lead-magnet) use the window named in their own vault note.

**Task conventions:**

- **Parent name:** experiment name without the date suffix, e.g. `Question-Format Subject Lines`.
- **Parent note:** one line of context (goal / next action), then a blank line, then the `obsidian://open?vault=MarkPKM&file=...` link to the vault note (URL-encode spaces as `%20`, slashes as `%2F`). Keep the depth in the vault note, not here.
- **No due date on the parent or the Execute subtask.** Only the Measure subtask carries a due date, and only once Execute is done.
- **No tags by default.** Flag the parent at review time if the experiment is the focus of the week (`Weekly Plan` tag is the equivalent signal).

**Weekly review mechanism:** during Sunday review, open the `Marketing Experiments` project and **flag 1-2 parents** to surface them for the week. Measure subtasks with a due date surface on their own.

**Completion:** when the Measure subtask is done, mark the parent complete and update the vault note's `Result` and `Learning` sections.

**Triggering:** when Mark says "new marketing experiment [name]", capture a **new parent task** (with the Execute → Measure subtasks) in the `Marketing Experiments` project — not a new project, not a new folder — and ask whether the vault note already exists or needs to be created.

### Triage-specific rules learned

- **Already-done items:** during triage, Mark sometimes reveals an inbox item is already complete. Mark it completed (`completed: true`) instead of moving it. Easier than a move-then-complete.
- **Ghost inbox items:** the inbox will contain some items with `status: dropped` that never fully cleared. Flag them to Mark but leave them alone. Cleanup happens in the OmniFocus app.
- **Tags during triage:** Mark occasionally tags at triage time (for example, `Weekly Plan` on items that belong in a weekly planning view). Triage skill supports `add_tags` per item, use it.
- **"Skip" means leave in inbox.** Don't drop, don't defer, just leave the item where it is so Mark can handle it manually.

---

## 2. Capture Conventions

- **Default destination: inbox.** Always, unless Mark explicitly names a project in the ask.
- Example triggers that still go to inbox: "add a task to call Sam", "drop this in OmniFocus"
- Example trigger that goes to a project: "add 'refactor login flow' to Website"
- Single captures proceed without confirmation.
- Batch captures (more than one task) get a confirmation step.
- Never infer a project from context. If Mark's wording is ambiguous, ask.

---

## 3. Roles and the Status-Tag Pull System (restructured 2026-06-14)

Mark runs a roles-pull system adapted from MacSparky's Roles workshop. Roles set the "what am I working on" axis; status tags set the Kanban lane. Tasks are "endeavours" in that language. This replaces the old flat planning/state tag scheme (the previous Bench / Consider Next / Quarterly Plan setup).

### Roles = folders

The three in-scope roles map one to one onto OmniFocus folders. Folder membership *is* the role, so there are no role tags.

| Role | Folder |
|---|---|
| Learner and Explorer | Learner and Explorer |
| APR Business Owner | APR Business Owner |
| YFL CTO | YFL CTO |

Family and Me are parked (not yet rolled in). Arete statements for each role live in [Self/Roles.md](../Self/Roles.md). They are the values filter for deciding what is worth pulling onto a given week.

### Status tags (the Kanban lanes)

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| *(untagged)* | **Idea / backlog.** The default. Anything without a status tag is an idea, not a commitment. |
| `Shelf` | Warm queue. On-deck, coming back soon. |
| `Next Week` | Committed for next week. The staging lane. |
| `Weekly Plan` | Committed for this week. The week's pool. |
| `Doing` | In progress right now. The active lane, and where the tight WIP limit lives. |
| `Waiting` | Blocked on someone else. A separate axis, not part of the pull flow. |

No `Done` tag. Completing the task in OmniFocus *is* done. Add one only if a draggable "done" board column is ever wanted.

### The pull flow

Backlog (untagged) to `Shelf` to `Next Week` to `Weekly Plan` to `Doing` to completed.

- **WIP limits.** The tight, meaningful limit lives on `Doing`, the active lane (start around 1 to 3). `Weekly Plan` carries a looser weekly commitment cap (around 5 to 7). Both apply only to discretionary endeavour work; Mark sets the numbers.
- **Pull into `Doing` as you start.** Day to day, move an item from `Weekly Plan` to `Doing` when you actually begin it, and out again when you stop or complete it. `Doing` is the honest "what am I touching right now" lane.
- **Recurring Operations tasks carry no status tag.** Analytics pulls, GSC export, blog refresh, and the like flow on their own recurrence plus due dates and never count against the WIP limit. They are maintenance throughput, not pulled endeavours.
- **Mid-week arrivals destined for next week get `Next Week`, never `Weekly Plan`.** This keeps the current week's board stable once it is set; the item joins this week only when Sunday promotes it.
- `Weekly Plan` is the canonical "this week" signal across all folders. Where the Marketing Experiments pattern (Section 1) says "flag to surface for the week," the `Weekly Plan` tag is the equivalent; flagging stays a compatible secondary highlight.

### The Sunday pull (weekly review event, done in the OmniFocus app)

1. Complete or clear what finished.
2. Promote `Next Week` into `Weekly Plan`.
3. Refill `Next Week` and `Shelf` from the backlog, up to the WIP limit.
4. Glance at the role mix: is any role starving?

The review is the forcing function. It is what keeps the backlog from breeding zombies (the old `Quarterly Plan` problem): quarter candidates simply sit as backlog or `Shelf` and get pulled forward when they are actually due, instead of wearing a sticky tag that never expires.

### Tag migration (applied 2026-06-14; supersedes the 2026-04-19 cleanup plan)

Done in OmniFocus on 2026-06-14:

- **Added:** `Shelf`, `Next Week`.
- **Kept:** `Weekly Plan` (now the WIP lane), `Waiting` (unchanged: blocked on someone else).
- **Folded into `Shelf`:** the 11 live tasks carrying `Consider Next` were re-tagged to `Shelf`; `Bench` had no tasks. Both tags set to `dropped`. `Bench` is retired because its old meaning ("paused") is the opposite of MacSparky's bench ("active this week").
- **Retired quarter tags:** `Quarterly Plan` and `Q2 2026` set to `dropped` and stripped from their 13 live tasks (which fall back to untagged backlog); the older quarter tags (`Q1`-`Q4 2025`, `Q3`/`Q4 2024`) were already dropped.
- Dropped tags are hidden, not hard-deleted, so they are recoverable; hard-delete in the app if wanted.
- 8 tasks in dropped/dead projects still carry the now-hidden old tags; left untouched per the ghost-item rule.

### Other existing tags (unchanged by this change)

- **Ideas & Reading themes:** `AI Exploration`, `Business Strategy`, `Tooling Curiosity`. Tag tasks inside the `Ideas & Reading` project (APR) to filter the parking lot by theme during monthly review.
- **GTD contexts:** `Phone Calls`, `Errands`, `Home`, `Office`, `Online`, `Communications`.
- **Recurrence cadence:** `Daily`, `Weekly`, `Monthly`, `Quarterly`, `SemiAnnually`, `Annually`.
- **Domain / utility:** `Health`, `Writing`, `Glossary`, `Checklist`, `Automate`. People / scope: `Family`, `Friends`. (The old `Heatlh` typo is already fixed.)
- **Leftover:** the `!Plan` grouping tag is still active but unused by this scheme; retire it whenever convenient.

---

## 4. Review Cadence (observed)

Pulled from project `reviewIntervalValue` / `reviewIntervalUnit` on 2026-04-19:

| Project | Folder | Interval |
|---|---|---|
| Me | Me | Every 4 days |
| Household | Family | Every 2 weeks |
| Husband | Family | Every 9 days |
| Father | Family | Every 23 days |
| Friendship | Me | Every 10 days |
| Important Reading Queue | Me | Weekly |
| Photography | Learner and Explorer | Every 2 weeks |
| Experiments | Learner and Explorer | Every 16 days |
| GenAI Cohort Launch | APR > Initiatives | Weekly |
| Drip → Cakemail Cleanup | APR > Initiatives | Every 2 weeks |
| Vendor & Tool Migrations | APR > Initiatives | Monthly |
| A-CSM Relaunch | APR > Initiatives | Every 2 weeks |
| Operations | APR | Weekly |
| Ideas & Reading | APR | Monthly |
| Marketing Experiments | APR | Weekly |
| YFL Other | YFL CTO | Every 23 days |

**Cadence pattern:** APR Initiatives + Operations + Marketing Experiments review weekly to bi-weekly; Ideas & Reading reviews monthly (it's a parking lot, not a commitment list). Personal/Family varies. Old subject-area APR projects (Business Evolution, Website, Ongoing Business, Pragmatic LLM Uses, Agile and AI, Ship30For30) all dropped 2026-05-31 in the mode-based restructure.

**Review is done in the OmniFocus app**, not via a skill. Skills may surface review-adjacent info when asked (e.g. "what's stalled") via `omnifocus-query`.

---

## 5. Focus / Perspective Use

### Confirmed 2026-04-19

- Mark uses two custom perspectives: **Weekly Plan** and **Quarterly Plan**. Both are general (not bucket-specific) and rarely used.
- **Focus is a nice-to-have, not a daily habit yet.** The `omnifocus-focus` skill ships minimal: set focus on a bucket folder, clear focus, show current focus. No perspective switching wired in yet.
- **Bucket to folder mapping for focus:**
    - "Focus on APR" → set focus on `APR Business Owner` folder
    - "Focus on YFL" → set focus on `YFL CTO` folder
    - "Focus on Personal/Family" → spans three folders (`Family`, `Me`, `Learner and Explorer`). The skill should ask which specific folder, or apply all three if the MCP supports multi-folder focus.
    - "Clear focus" → reset

Revisit perspective integration once Mark actually starts using focus regularly.

### Kanban status board (added 2026-06-14)

The status tags from Section 3 (`Shelf`, `Next Week`, `Weekly Plan`, `Doing`) are designed to drive a custom perspective grouped by tag. That grouping is the Kanban board, one column per lane. Filter it to a single folder for a one-role board, or leave it across all three folders for the whole picture. OmniFocus 4 has no native board view, so tag-grouping is the approximation. Repoint the existing "Weekly Plan" perspective at this scheme; the "Quarterly Plan" perspective can be retired along with the quarter tags.

---

## 6. Recurrence (repeating tasks and projects)

The MCP supports recurrence on both tasks and projects. Use `create_tasks` / `create_projects` to seed the task, then apply recurrence via `update_tasks` / `update_projects` (the create calls don't take recurrence fields directly as of 2026-04-20).

### Fields

- `recurrence` — an iCalendar RRULE string, or `""` to clear recurrence.
- `repetition_method` — how the next occurrence is scheduled:
    - `fixed` — next occurrence is calculated from the *original* schedule, regardless of when it's completed. Best for rhythms that should happen on a consistent day (weekly review, monthly bills).
    - `start_after_completion` — next defer date is X after you actually complete it. Best for tasks where the gap between completions matters more than the date (water the plants, lubricate the bike chain).
    - `due_after_completion` — next due date is X after you actually complete it. Similar to above but for due-dated tasks.

### Common RRULEs

| Cadence | RRULE |
|---|---|
| Every day | `FREQ=DAILY;INTERVAL=1` |
| Every weekday | `FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,TU,WE,TH,FR` |
| Weekly | `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1` |
| Every 2 weeks | `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=2` |
| Monthly | `FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=1` |
| Quarterly | `FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=3` |
| Annually | `FREQ=YEARLY;INTERVAL=1` |

### Default choices

- **Rhythms (weekly review, analytics pull, reviews)** → `repetition_method: fixed` so the cadence stays consistent.
- **Maintenance tasks (chores, bike tune-up, HVAC filter)** → `repetition_method: start_after_completion` so the clock resets on completion.
- **Due-dated tasks (bill pay, quarterly filing)** → `repetition_method: due_after_completion`.

### Reading recurrence from a task

The `get_tasks` response includes `isRecurring`, `recurrence` (RRULE), `repetitionMethod`, and `repeatSummary` (human-readable, always prefer this for display). `nextDueDate` / `nextDeferDate` are populated for recurring tasks.

### Safe update pattern

```python
update_tasks(tasks=[{
    "id": task_id,
    "recurrence": "FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1",
    "repetition_method": "fixed"
}])
```

Clearing recurrence: `recurrence: ""`.

---

## 7. Skill Safety Rails (applies to all)

- **Reads:** no confirmation needed.
- **Single writes** (one task create, one task update): proceed immediately, report result.
- **Batch writes** (more than one task affected): show the plan, wait for approval.
- **Deletes:** always confirm. Prefer `drop` over `delete` unless Mark says "permanently delete."
- **Recurring task completion:** use the MCP's proper completion mechanism, never a raw "set completed to true" pattern. The MCP handles next-occurrence generation.

---

## 8. Cowork Bridge Notes

- The OmniFocus MCP runs on Mark's Mac. From Cowork, the `mcp__omnifocus__*` tools call into it directly.
- If the MCP is disconnected, the skills can't run. Tell Mark to restart Claude Desktop / re-enable the MCP.
- Rich data is available via MCP; no need for pasted output or dump files.

---

*Last updated: 2026-06-16 (Marketing Experiments Do → Measure subtask structure + measurement-window defaults; Section 1). Update this doc whenever conventions change. The skills read it at runtime to stay aligned.*

  - process my inbox

---

# Drafts Inbox

Triage the items sitting in the Drafts **inbox** — your capture-to-action pipeline. Archiving each item when it's handled means the inbox itself is the "unprocessed since last run" queue; there's no separate timestamp to track.

## When to Use

Use this skill at the start of a session or whenever you want to process items you've captured throughout the day via Drafts on iPhone, Apple Watch, or Mac.

## Prerequisites

- Drafts MCP connector must be set up.

## Instructions

1. Read the inbox with `drafts_get_drafts` (`folder: "inbox"`). This returns summaries only (title, dates, flags, tags), not full content.
2. **Check the volume first.** If the inbox is large (more than ~20 items, i.e. a backlog rather than a session's worth), don't try to process everything blindly. Report the count and date range, and ask how far back to go (e.g. this month, last 3 months, flagged only, or the whole backlog). Default to the most recent window.
   - The MCP returns the full inbox; use the `modificationDate` field to filter to the chosen window yourself. `drafts_get_drafts` also accepts `modifiedAfter` / `flagged` to narrow the pull.
3. Present a numbered list of the in-scope items with a brief preview of each.
4. For each item, pull its full content with `drafts_get_draft` (the summary title is truncated), classify it, and take the appropriate action:

| Type | Action |
|------|--------|
| **Task or to-do** | Capture to OmniFocus via `omnifocus-capture` (inbox by default). Flag if urgent. |
| **Writing idea (substantial)** | Create a Writing Task in `APR/TaskNotes/Tasks/` (frontmatter: `status`, `priority`, `dateCreated`/`dateModified`, `tags: [task]`, `ContentType: Blog`/`Newsletter`/`Glossary`). |
| **Content hook (one-liner)** | Add to the running `APR/Efforts/Content Ideas.md` note. |
| **Research request** | Do the research and report findings. |
| **Quick instruction** | Execute the instruction (file a note, move a file, look something up). |
| **Question** | Answer the question. |
| **Reference / clipping** | File it where it belongs (vault note, DevonThink, etc.) or note that it's already captured elsewhere. |
| **Unclear** | Ask for clarification before acting. |

5. After processing each item, archive the draft with `drafts_archive`.
6. Report what was done: "[N] items processed. [Brief summary of actions taken.]"

## Rules

- Process items one at a time. Don't batch everything silently. (For a large backlog, a grouped proposal with a per-item action is fine, but get approval before archiving or capturing anything.)
- When an item is ambiguous, ask rather than guess.
- Archive each draft only after it's been fully processed — the archive is what marks it "done," so never archive something you skipped.
- If an item requires a tool you don't have access to, note it and move on (leave it in the inbox).
- Confirm before deleting; default to archive, not trash.

---

*Started with the Robot Assistant Field Guide Starter Kit. Customized in Video 6 via the assembler. Updated 2026-06-28 to triage the whole inbox instead of a "cowork" tag.*

content.text:
{
  "id": "D6A5B311-3274-4AD8-9F68-EAC2E268F603",
  "title": "Canada has a real productivity problem. We have for decades. In 1984, the Canadian economy was 88% as productive as the US per hour worked. In 2022, it had fallen to 71%.",
  "content": "Canada has a real productivity problem. We have for decades. In 1984, the Canadian economy was 88% as productive as the US per hour worked. In 2022, it had fallen to 71%.

The new AI strategy is an attempt to fix that. It promises a 3 percent increase in GDP, from labour productivity. "Increase Canada's business adoption of AI from 12 percent today to 60 percent by 2034, through boosting SMEs and business adoption supports." I'm reminded of the mineshaft gap in Dr Strangelove. Adoption of AI doesn’t make an organization more productive. 

Saying a new technology will magically make us more productive, doesn’t make it so.

## Sectors
The strategy names all sorts of sectors where AI will create: "outsized value..." - why those sectors? Based on what evidence.

1. Health - improve Health Outcomes with AI? Where would we use AI and what evidence is there to support that it helps?
2. Energy and Natural Resources: AI used to optimize extraction and accelerate clean energy transformation? How
3. Transportation ...

There are many ways AI could help and harm in all of these sectors. The strategy is too vague to be useful here.

## Healthcare
I will focus on the health sector. In Ontario, we constantly hear stories of emergency rooms overflowing. In some rural communities, the emergency rooms operate on reduced hours due to staffing shortages. To make the emergency room more efficient, we might try to use AI to help in the triage process. Assuming the AI doesn't make any mistakes (unwise assumption), we've sped up the triage process. Unfortunately if the hospital is operating at 100% or more of capacity in terms of the number of beds, speeding triage doesn’t help. So speeding triage might help a few people leave emergency faster but it doesn't make a meaningful difference.

Our mistake? We tackled the emergency room problem in isolation. 

Putting on our Systems Thinking hat, we want to ask two questions:
- Why are there so many people visiting emergency rooms?
- Why are hospital beds so full?

### Hospital beds
- Low population to hospital bed ratio
- Waiting lists for long term care
- Staffing shortages

### Emergency Room Volume
- Lack of family doctor
- Lack of family doctor turns simple problems into more complex problems, which in turn might result in a hospital stay
- Unsure where to go - walk in clinic? Emergency?
- Seasonal flu et al

None of these problems will magically get fixed by AI. If we want our healthcare system to help us get well/stay well, look at the overall system. 

One example of hospital taking a systemic approach? Humber River Hospital has a command centre where they're paying attention[1] to:
- Emergency Department volume
- Bed allocations and assignments
- Room cleaning
- Critical care capacity
- Surgical scheduling
- Discharge planning

Reading the promotional PDF from GE the command centre is focused on getting the patients who need admission a bed faster and reducing pain, complications and secondary infections.

GE promotes this system as using AI, however the AI isn't the central feature. The value of this system is that people in the hospital are paying constant attention to how the hospital is working. If there is a constraint, they make changes to reduce the problem. The command centre is staffed by a cross disciplinary group of people, so that they there is enough knowledge in the room to make good decisions.

AI is useful here, because they've studied the flow of the system. They've established useful metrics: getting people healthy and allowing them to leave hospital. In this context, using an AI to find patterns and help make short term predictions seems very useful. GenAI is good at finding patterns.

The material available in public is promotional so the actual effectiveness of the real system is something I can't see.

AI didn't make Humber River Hospital more effective. Improving the flow in the system made it more effective, GenAI is just a tool in this picture.

### Family Doctors and GenAI
Earlier we noted that the lack of family doctors is a contributing factor to over capacity. 

One of the challenges that they face, after a day of seeing patients they need to write up charts documenting their findings, treatment and prescriptions. This is unpaid labour, the doctor is paid for the patient visit and the documentation is treated as overhead.

Family doctors are already dealing with burnout, it turns out that OHIPs payments in many cases don't cover the realistic costs of running a clinic (rental, front office staff, medical equipment, computers, etc.) When your business struggles financially, it's no surprise that doing charts is seen as an added burden.

Many doctors I know have turned to GenAI transcription tools. There are clearly documented problems with some of these tools making mistakes with both the names of problems and medications. Yet the physicians I know report saving a considerable amount of time with few, if any, errors.

GenAI might help here, however we've solved a symptom. Family doctors are expected to run businesses (not their training) and are expected to handle a large number of administrative tasks along with seeing patients.

Transcription tools may help, but they don’t solve the underlying problem. The administrative burden on family doctors is a major factor in their burnout.

## Not a Magic Wand
GenAI isn't a magic wand and it isn't a panacea. In the right context, it can be a very useful. Used in the wrong place, it can be a disaster.

Humber River Hospital’s command centre is a good step in the right direction. If we want to make a meaningful difference in the healthcare system, we need to look a bigger than just an emergency room. In short look, it would seem we want to understand why family doctors are leaving the profession. If we can't keep them happy to stay in the profession, then we can't expect to keep patients out of the emergency room. At the other end of the spectrum, since many hospital beds are occupied by patients waiting for a long term care, we need to find compassionate ways to improve the long term care system. We may also need more hospital staff and more beds. 

The Healthcare system in Canada is just one example of many. We have a productivity problems, but we can’t just tell people to use GenAI and expect an improvement. If want to improve productivity, we need to look at each organization as a system, understand the bottlenecks in the system and focus on eliminating that bottleneck.

  "id": "A6860D5B-7379-48FE-9E9B-2101D941E4EC",
  "title": "July 3 - I called Videotron to get an eSim for my new phone. Two things happened:",
  "content": "July 3 - I called Videotron to get an eSim for my new phone. Two things happened:
- My previous phone used a physical SIM card and I was told that the eSim would be sent to my home today.
- I was told my existing contract could not be transferred to an eSim and that I was being offered a new contract with more data for the slightly cheaper price.

July 4 - I get en email from Videotron telling me that I have a new contract. However, the PDF is password protected and I don’t have the password. I ignored it, since I assumed the contract is already in place.

July 7 - 4pm My old phone, with the physical SIM card, lost cell service and I see no sign of the eSim. Everyone in my family is getting messages from Videotron about having reached their data limit: "Your Mobile account's data overage fees are currently at $46.02. The data overage fee limit on the Videotron and Videotron partner networks is set at $50 for all the lines on your account. For the current billing cycle, the following Mobile Line(s) are affected: 613-299-5650."

6:45 pm The eSim is resolved. Following up on my last conversation. I have spent 2 hours and 30 minutes driving to and from a Videotron store in Gatineau to get an eSim. When I contacted Videotron on July 3, I was told that the eSim would be sent to my home. The person at the Videotron store told me that doesn’t work and that no matter what I was going to be forced to visit a Videotron store.

I still need resolution on the following issues:
- Why is the phone: 613-299-5650 - getting messages about data overage fees? Their plan has 3GB a month. They're very careful with their data usage. User Centre claims that this phone has no data allowance. How is that possible?
- How do we fix this problem?
- Between cancelling my evening appointments and 2 hours and 30 minutes of driving and now further time spent with Videotron customer service, I would like a credit for one month's service for my family.

Between all of the phone calls, chats and driving to and from the Videotron store, I've now spent 4 hours on this.

July 8 - more than another hour on chat with Videotron. Result: Everyone gets 100GB of data per month. Price goes up by $10/mth. I get a $50 credit for my trouble.

{
  "id": "860BEADB-FDFF-4E57-9F41-796D9864A4D1",
  "title": "Reshuffle",
  "content": "Reshuffle

The music industry is a good example of the change that is being unleashed by AI.

Music came in albums and required a record company's backing because of the pressing costs for the vinyl and the need for distribution network.

Digital music reduces those costs and so albums become less important and singles more important.

Spotify, Apple Music et al, become arise because they become the way people find music.

In the process much of the old music industry died.
--
Using Shein, with all of it's flaws, as another example - the work heirarchy has been completely inverted. There aren't long meetings about reducing risk. There aren't seasonal cycles, they run small experiments, if an item takes off they do more, if it fails they look for another.experiment.

There are no silos and limited coordination overhead.

Ignoring the ethical and environmental implications of the way they do business, they're a very agile organization.

Shein's success isn't about doing individual tasks faster, but deliver the outcomes that the audience wants sooner.
--
## Ch 5 Rebundling the Job
Core claim - in a world where everyone has access to the same knowledge, there is knowledge overwhelm.

The promise of good taste and curation beats the promise of volume.

Leans into Theory of Constraints with a twist. Constraints are Scarcity, Risk and Coordination.

**Scarcity** - something that is a key resource is limited. In the case of shipping he shows that communications with the outside world - to keep up to date on schedule or summon help in emergency. So the radio operator with Morse code was the constraint. In modern software development the constraint is often Quality Assurance or Code Review.

**Risks** - Anaesthesiologist in a surgical environment. They're managing risk in the surgery. Paying attention to the patient's vital signs. Too much anaesthetic and the patients organs will shut down. Too little and they will wake up in the midst of the surgery.

**Coordination** - Many moving parts that need to align across groups. The book's example is getting a movie made. From writing, actors, sets, costumes, cinematography, funding, editing and ... . In this world the Producer is the coordinator and the becomes the constraint.

When all wine, good, bad and awful became more widely available the value of the sommelier increased. Wine is no longer scarce. Further, the internet is full of reviews about wine and vineyards. The constraint now is knowing where to look and who to trust. The sommelier is curating and instilling confidence. A restaurant uses them now as part of a package, promising people a better dining experience.

### Don't Chase the Skill, Follow the Constraint
Up skilling is still valuable, but only in the context of understanding the constraints first. Look to where the scarcity, risk or coordination constraints are and up skill for those problems.

> Skills are only valuable in relation to solving a constraint.

The evolution of the role of radiologists is a good example. They go from interpreting scans, to providing context for their colleagues. A shadow on a lung has a different meaning depending on the history of a patient. They participate more in the discussion of how to treat a cancer. *The implied claim that AI would get better than humans at reading X-ray and other images, still hasn't panned out.*

When constraints change, the roles that had value in the old case lose value. However, new roles emerge to tackle the new constraints.

The core claim of the book thus far: AI unbundles some tasks. Work that used to be valuable is no longer valuable. Instead of scarcity of skills, the constraints will be handling risk and coordination.

**Risks** with a new technology, we look for risks within the technology itself. Example elevators, the first question is what happens if the technology fails, will the elevator fall? The bigger risks come from the downstream effects. Elevators enable tall buildings, which have new structural and fire risks.

With GenAI one of the added layers of risk is the probabilistic nature of the systems.

**Coordination** tells a story of nurse navigators, helping patients deal with the increasingly messy journey through the hospital system. They use their expertise to coordinate. In the process they reduce the stress level for the patient and shorten the hospital stay.

The AI tools made some areas/departments work faster, but they were silos. The author calls this narrow. The nurse coordinator is working broadly across the whole system.

*We get to this better place, by helping people see the whole system and not the parts.*

==We only get rewarded when the value is made visible. It's not enough to improve the system if people don't see the value created.==

*Tidbit* - As AI execution scales, handling the exceptions (i.e. mislabel bins, damaged parts) becomes a much larger and more important job. The people who do this work in a warehouse do it informally and so are rarely noticed. It shows up in care environments, the system pays people for the task, yet the biggest value is the emotional support they provide.

Part of reimagining work will require making the invisible work (value?), visible to the system.

## Ch 6 Rebundling the Organization
Real Madrid, mid 2000s, built around star players. All given autonomy, yet they produced mediocre results. They optimized for individual play and didn't have a system. Barcelona, succeeded by having a system and giving players freedom within their zone.

The more complex the system, the more specialized the parts, the more important for there to be an explicit coordination system. Real Madrid failed because they lacked a system.

Mars Climate Orbiter is another example of coordination failure. One team did their math in pound-force and the other Newtons. Each team trusted the others competence and didn't question the numbers, they were experts after all. Small errors accumulated. The navigation system believed it was in the right place. When it tried to enter orbit, it instead hit the thin atmosphere and burned up. The teams had worked in isolation.

### Reducing the Coordination Tax with AI
The author claims that AI eliminates the tax. I'm troubled because he's ignoring the possibility of hallucination and the biases that the AI will add in.

He cites NotebookLLM, good. But also Persona generation. Not so good.

Leaning very heavily into Agentic execution to scout out and book sales calls -> agents to select suppliers.

Another good example is that burden of expense reporting has gone away. An AI pulls receipts from inboxes, categorizes and then sends them to the right people for approval. *Neither the employee, nor finance are dealing with the mess of expenses. A coordination tax has been eliminated*

The AI helps us when it aids the teams/organization to manage its own coordination. It enslaves us when it tells us what to do.

When we use AI in a narrow context i.e. within a single team, the team might go faster but the coordination tax goes up. Because the team using the AI produces more stuff than the other teams can handle. *This is classic Scrum deployment problem. A scrum team might significantly outpace the rest of the organization.*

> AI tool providers increasingly sell us: That AI will revolutionize knowledge work the way industrial automation revolutionized manufacturing. But there is a problem: knowledge work isn't like factory work.

Helping different teams coordinate their work, handle dependencies, work at different speeds and for different goals. This is where we need help.

Speed is not progress; Automation is not transformation.

## Ch 7. Rebundling the Value Chain

### Building Blocks on rent
The author makes the pitch that we more and more of what we need to build a business can be rented, as a series of building of blocks.

*Not super impressed with this section, where uses Mr Beast's Burger fiasco as a good and bad example*

Renting building blocks is ok to a point, what happens to quality? In addition, I can't see how this relates to AI.

# Section 3 Competitive Advantage 
## Ch 8 The Tool Integration Trap

{
  "id": "D20C94B2-70EC-475E-A45A-5D6C016C3594",
  "title": "Imagine giving a Feature Factory a superpower. Not the power to understand customers better. Not the power to measure outcomes. The power to ship features faster.",
  "content": "Imagine giving a Feature Factory a superpower. Not the power to understand customers better. Not the power to measure outcomes. The power to ship features faster.\n\nThat's what GenAI does for teams already stuck in the output trap.\n\nThe original Feature Factory symptoms: rigid roadmaps, no discovery, velocity obsession, ignored tech debt. None of them were caused by building too slowly. They were caused by not stopping to think. AI doesn't fix that. It removes the last natural speed bump that might have forced a conversation about value.\n\nWhen code was expensive to write, teams at least had to prioritize. When AI makes it cheap, everything gets built. The backlog becomes a conveyor belt.\n\nSo what's the antidote? Same as it always was focus outcomes but now AI can actually help.\n\nScrumMasters: push for experiment-driven Sprints. Instead of \"build feature X,\" frame the Sprint Goal as \"learn whether X solves problem Y.\" Use AI to stand up a quick prototype or Fake Door MVP to test the hypothesis.\n\nProduct Owners: use the speed AI gives you to validate faster, not ship faster. Run three small experiments in the time it used to take to build one feature.\n\nAI is a superpower. The question is whether you use it to produce more, or to learn faster.\n\nhttps://agilepainrelief.com/blog/gen-ai-and-the-feature-factory-automating-away-collaboration/",

  "title": "**Prompt:**",
  "content": "
**Prompt:**

I'm building a strategic overview of my business, Agile Pain Relief Consulting. The attached file (`strategic-business-overview.md`) was generated by analyzing my website repository: course pages, 174 blog posts, 158 glossary entries, analytics reports, marketing experiment results, and content strategy documents. It represents what can be learned from the public-facing side of the business.

Your job is to search this Obsidian vault for private information that the website analysis could not capture, and produce an updated version of the strategic overview (or a companion addendum) that fills in the gaps. Specifically, look for notes, conversations, reflections, and planning documents that address:

**Priority questions (Section 10 of the attached file):**

1. **Effective Scrum**: Any notes on why it stalled. Was there feedback from prospects? Did you test messaging variants? Notes on the self-paced + group coaching format. Any thinking about pivoting the format to a different topic (GenAI, leadership, etc.).

2. **AI/GenAI course planning**: Any notes on course design, target audience, format decisions, certification partnerships, pricing thinking, or timeline.

3. **Post-training community**: Notes on what was tried with the forum, why it failed, ideas for replacements, or observations about what attendees actually want after training.

4. **Word-of-mouth dynamics**: Client conversations, referral patterns, notes on how people find you, what triggers them to recommend you, any referral program ideas.

5. **Revenue and pricing**: Actual price points for courses, revenue breakdowns between public courses and private/consulting work, seasonal patterns, historical revenue trends.

6. **Capacity and team**: Notes on bringing on other trainers, what worked or didn't, capacity constraints, burnout considerations, delegation experiments.

7. **Client retention and upsell**: Data or observations on whether CSM grads progress to A-CSM/CSP-SM, typical client journeys, lifetime value estimates.

8. **Competitive landscape**: Notes on competitors, pricing comparisons, differentiation thinking, market positioning relative to others.

9. **Partnerships**: Scrum Alliance relationship details, conference networks, content partnerships, co-training arrangements.

10. **Email/Drip strategy**: Campaign performance, open rates, conversion rates, list growth, nurture sequences, what emails drive course registrations.

11. **Consulting work**: Types of engagements, typical clients, revenue contribution, whether this is growing or shrinking, strategic role of consulting vs. training.

12. **Personal energy and priorities**: Notes on what energizes Mark vs. what drains him, time allocation preferences, what he wants the business to look like in 3-5 years.

13. **Market trends and industry observations**: Notes on the state of Agile/Scrum adoption, whether the market is growing or contracting, how GenAI is changing demand for training.

**What to produce:**

- For each of the 13 areas above, report what you found in the vault (with note titles/dates where possible) and what remains unknown.
- Where vault information contradicts or adds nuance to the website analysis, flag it explicitly.
- Update or extend the SWOT analysis (Section 9) with anything new.
- Add any strategic tensions, opportunities, or risks that are visible from the vault but invisible from the website.
- If you find strategic thinking, business model experiments, or product ideas that aren't captured in the attached file at all, add a new section for them.

Do not rewrite the entire document. Produce a structured addendum that I can read alongside the original, organized by the 13 areas above plus any new sections. Be direct about what the vault reveals and where gaps remain even after this analysis.
--
Only search inside of /APR for now

- Blog
- Glossary

- Newsletter archive is incomplete and will be added to later
- Scrum Alliance Course Click-through rate is out of date and likely won’t be updated.

  "id": "3E5A84BC-DC24-4E73-BE97-7CEFAC51E638",
  "title": "BDD notes",
  "content": "BDD notes

- One paper was around testing UI PostHoc - well done and not useful.
See Panda Post
- Has anyone written a good BDD discovery coach. Could I turn the example mapping blog post into a discovery tool?
- Automating creation of Playwright tests and also **interpreting results**
- BDD collaboration - most important in cases of: complexity; Regulatory; Legacy

Current generation reasoning relies on statistical pattern matching. Reasoning responses are often just replicating patterns seen in training data. This is not a logical deduction.

Code and architectural quality in general, Models suffer in their attempts to create good quality code:
- trained on a mass of code across the internet -> No coherent principles involved
- training data isn't grounded in OO, Functional Programming or any other principles -> can be added by use "skills" et al however this is a context consuming band-aid
- May follow unconventional patterns making it harder to understand
- Doesn't know the problem domain it's being asked to work in.
- Doesn't have access to all of the relevant data. Code, User Stories, etc and not all stored in the same place. In addition they're often not written in the same language 
- Context windows are still a problem - even models with large context windows often 'forget' to pay attention to the bits in the middle

10 yrs ago, we all knew not to blindly paste StackOverflow code into our products. Now we do that every day and call it productivity.

1	# Social posts — week of 2026-06-15 (next-few-days batch)
2	
3	Working draft. **Rewrite the posts marked `REWRITE`** (the blog + 2 course posts) in your own voice; leave the `READY` ones or tweak as you like. When you're done, tell me and I'll convert this into the 3-platform batch JSON at `analytics/social-media-content-evergreen/next-few-days.json`, condensing each post to LinkedIn / Mastodon (<=500) / Bluesky (<=290).
4	
5	Conventions when I build the JSON: the URL goes in the `url` field (no UTM, no inline links; the pipeline adds per-platform UTM), and `image` stays `""` (the pipeline scrapes og:image).
6	
7	**Posting order:** the pipeline schedules in array order, 3 posts/weekday at 10:00, 13:30, 15:30 ET. The order below interleaves AI and Scrum so no day is all one theme. Reorder by moving blocks.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## 1. Blog — false consensus — REWRITE
12	**URL:** /blog/gen-ai-wont-speed-up-your-scrum-events-and-shouldnt/
13	
14	You hand the team a clean list of GenAI-generated user stories.
15	
16	They read them. They nod. They say "yes, I understand."
17	
18	And every person is picturing something different.
19	
20	That's the trap with using GenAI to write your user stories, epics, or acceptance criteria. These artifacts were never the point. They exist to help people to reach a shared understanding through conversation. When the story arrives looking finished, the conversation never happens, and you get false agreement that falls apart as soon as the work starts.
21	
22	This predates GenAI. Product Owners could always bash out a polished product backlog item and mistake nodding for understanding. GenAI just manufactures that false consensus faster.
23	
24	Where can GenAI help in Refinement: ask it to pressure-test a story. Does it meet INVEST? Is the "why" clear? Where's the ambiguity? Stuck splitting something big? Have it suggest splits. Most of them will be wrong, but it can be a good spark. Let it question your prioritization.
25	
26	The difference: those uses spark the conversation. Generating the stories replaces it.
27	
28	I use these tools daily. Knowing where they erode shared understanding is how you use them well.
29	
30	How GenAI fits across all five Scrum events and activities:
31	
32	#AIinSoftwareDevelopment #ProductOwner
33	
34	---
35	
36	## 2. Evergreen — Daily Scrum — READY
37	**URL:** /blog/modern-guide-to-daily-scrum-meeting/
38	
39	The Daily Scrum isn't a status meeting, and the moment it becomes one, it dies.
40	
41	Three people reciting yesterday-today-blockers at a ScrumMaster is reporting, not planning. The point is the team re-planning the day together toward the Sprint Goal: what we learned, what changed, where we help each other.
42	
43	If yours feels like a chore, the format is the problem, not the people.
44	
45	#Scrum #ScrumMaster
46	
47	---
48	
49	## 3. Quiz — confidence trap — READY
50	**URL:** /quiz/ai-failure-modes/
51	
52	Microsoft researchers (2025) found something uncomfortable: the more confident an LLM sounds, the less critical thinking people apply to what it says.
53	
54	Confidence is the trap, and it's only one of the failure modes quietly shaping how teams build software right now.
55	
56	How well do you know the AI Failure Modes hitting Development Teams? Test yourself. Twelve questions, three minutes.
57	
58	#AIinSoftwareDevelopment
59	
60	---
61	
62	## 4. Course — glass 1/3 full — REWRITE
63	**URL:** /surviving-the-ai-tsunami-an-evidenced-based-course/
64	
65	Most of the AI conversation hands you two options.
66	
67	The glass is overflowing: AI replaces your engineers next year, so go as fast as you can. Or the glass is empty: it's all hype and harm, avoid it.
